title: Beat A World Champion At THIS Puzzle
description:
*** THE SUDOKU EVENT OF THE YEAR ***
Huge news:  Phistomefel's first ever sudoku hunt is OUT!!! We've gifted it as a Christmas present to all our patrons to say "Thank you" for supporting us. 

We've also got Jay Dyer's sudoku hunt - Numeric Alchemy - coming TOMORROW (and this is another EXTRAORDINARY thing!)

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
WHAT A PUZZLE this is today from Stefan Liew.  It's called Outside: Castle Wall and it's a loop-building problem from the website:

www.gmpuzzles.com

Not only is this an incredible puzzle but it has an interesting story attached to it.  This is one of the only puzzles on that site that former World Puzzle Champion, Thomas Snyder, solved in more than the "Expert" time standard (which was 45 minutes).  You simply must have a go at this to see if you can best him!

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rFRF94qjg3

Rules: 
Draw a single closed loop (without intersections or crossings) passing through some empty cells in the grid. Cells with arrows/numbers are not part of the loop. The numbers and arrows refer to the total sum of the lengths of loop segments in the given direction. (An equivalent way to understand these values is to count the number of cell borders crossed by the loop in that direction.)

title: The Best 40th Birthday Present
description:
*** THE SUDOKU EVENT OF THE YEAR ***
Huge news:  Phistomefel's first ever sudoku hunt is OUT!!! We've gifted it as a Christmas present to all our patrons to say "Thank you" for supporting us. 

We've also got Jay Dyer's sudoku hunt - Numeric Alchemy - coming on 1 January (and this is another EXTRAORDINARY thing!)

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fabulous 40th birthday present today created by the_cogito for one of our stream moderators Tristan.  This is a really clever puzzle - themed heavily around the number 40 - and somehow it resolves itself uniquely.  Better than a Ferrari?  We'll let you decide!

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/99JFmbth6r

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every row, column and 3x3 box contains exactly one "doubler" cell. A digit in a doubler cell counts for twice its value for the purposes of all cage sums. Digits in doubler cells form a unique set of the digits 1 to 9. Digits may not repeat in cages, though values might. (eg a cage may not contain a doubled 2 and a regular 2 but may contain a doubled 2 and a regular 4). Caged cells must sum to the value indicated in the top left corner of the cage. The cell with a grey circle contains an odd digit. The cell with the grey square contains an even digit.

title: Under Pressure: The Sudoku
description:
*** THE SUDOKU EVENT OF THE YEAR ***
Huge news:  Phistomefel's first ever sudoku hunt is OUT!!! We've gifted it as a Christmas present to all our patrons to say "Thank you" for supporting us. 

We can also announce that Jay Dyer's sudoku hunt, Numeric Alchemy, will be our January reward - coming on New Years Day!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have to be honest: we were scared of this puzzle's ruleset - which is barmy - but it's been recommended to us and the list of names who've loved this puzzle reads like a pantheon of sudoku greats.  So here is Under Pressure by AnalyticalNinja and the highest compliment we can pay it is that we think Freddie would have liked it.

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GDmnmRhFgN

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. All cages are “aquariums”. Cells within aquariums are either air cells or water cells, with cells outside of cages not being air or water. Water cells fill the bottoms of cages and must have digits greater than all the air cells in their cage. Rows in cages must be either all air cells or all water cells. Cages must have at least one row of air cells and one row of water cells. Additionally, the cages are “pressurized”: The air cells within any cage must have a higher average value than the number of rows above that cage in the grid. (Eg If a cage occupied only rows 7, 8 and 9 then any air cells in that cage must have an average value greater than 6.)

An example can be found here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000CDX

title: A Sudoku With Only Six Empty Circles?!
description:
*** THE SUDOKU EVENT OF THE YEAR ***
Huge news:  Phistomefel's first ever sudoku hunt is OUT!!! We've gifted it as a Christmas present to all our patrons to say "Thank you" for supporting us. 

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The return of an old Master to the channel today in the form of Mark Sweep (aka Frostini) and his puzzle Nurimisaki Sudoku - a hybrid of the Nikoli logic problem Nurinisaki and our old "friend" sudoku.  This is simply superb so do try to give it a go if you have time!

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GjDNNTdp4r

Rules: 
Normal sudoku and Nurimisaki rules apply. In addition, orthogonally adjacent cells along the Nurimisaki path (unshaded cells) have a difference of at least 5. Nurimisaki Rules are as follows: Shade some cells so that the remaining unshaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 region may be entirely shaded or unshaded. Circles mark every instance of a cell which is unshaded and orthogonally adjacent to exactly one other unshaded cell (i.e. the circles are the only ‘endpoints’ of the unshaded area). The digit in a circle indicates how many cells are in the straight line of unshaded cells coming out of the cell with the circle, including itself.

description:
Here's where you can play Merry Camel to You! by Panthera: https://tinyurl.com/3cnj2c7n 
Irregular/region sudoku rules apply. The are 4 6x6 grids (separated by the cages) that each use the digits 1-6 each. Japanese sums rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are Red, White (green clues), Blue, and Pink. Red and white clues appear on the top and left side of the grid, while blue and pink appear on the right and bottom. There are no unshaded cells. The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs found in that row or column that must be shaded the color of the clue (green clues represent white!). If a clue is black, then both colors must be present in the row or column. There must be a different color between runs of the same color. If a row or column is unclued, those colors do not appear in that row or column. Clues read left to right (or top to bottom) in both cases.

A very Merry Christmas to one and all! We celebrate with an absolute belter of a puzzle from ThePedallingPianist called Rudolph?  It has a bonkers ruleset and is a complete joy from start to finish... is there even a festive joke going on?

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JMphTDjnGG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The line is an “equal sums” line, meaning that digits on the line have an equal sum, N, within each 3x3 box through which it passes. So, for example, r4c2+r5c2+r6c2 = r4c8+r5c8+r5c7. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one digit has double the value of the other). There are nine 'quintupler' cells in the grid, coloured red. They contain the digits 1-9 exactly once each, and occupy exactly one position in each row, column and 3x3 box. For the purpose of any arithmetic calculations, digits in quintupler cells count as five times the digit's value.

title: A Special Pie for Xmas Eve
description:
Here's where you can try Seven Fish Pie by Missing a few Cards: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2N2TgTPLjf 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a green line, adjacent digits have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a purple line form a consecutive sequence, in any order. Digits along the thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits joined by white dots are consecutive; those joined by black dots have a 2:1 ratio. Not all dots are given.

The Fish Pie Recipe is as follows:
Seven Fish Pie
This is the recipe that inspired the Feast of the Seven Fishes puzzle. It is our traditional Christmas Eve
dinner. As with many great recipes, there is flexibility with some of the amounts and ingredients.

INGREDIENTS
For the cheeses in the sauce and topping, we usually use a good parmesan, English cheddar, or
combination of the two but you can experiment with other varieties.
For the Sauce
1 shallot
2 tablespoons butter
1 tablespoon flour
1/2 cup (125 mL) heavy cream
1/2 cup (125 mL) milk
paprika
sriracha spice
turmeric
salt
pepper
chives
2-3 oz (60-70g) cheese
frozen peas
frozen corn
The Fish
The total amount of fish should be about 4 oz (115g) per person, or a bit more. Use a combination of fish,
ideally seven different types that complement each other. Some of our favorites include:

Arctic char
Ocean perch
Cod
Haddock
Shrimp
For the Topping
3 large russet potatoes

2 tablespoons butter
1/2 cup (125 mL) heavy cream
2-3 oz (60-70g) cheese

DIRECTIONS
Preheat the oven to 450°F (230°C)
Peel and chop the potatoes. Place in cold, well-salted water, bring to a boil, and cook until tender. Drain, then mash with butter and cream. Stir in the grated cheese.
Mince the shallot very finely, and cook it over medium-high heat in butter. Add the flour, and stir to cook the flour until it is light brown and has a slightly nutty aroma. Add paprika, a little sriracha, and turmeric.
Slowly stir in the cream and the milk to form a roux. Cook, stirring, over medium-low heat. Add salt, pepper, and chives. Stir in the grated cheese. Just before assembling the dish for baking, stir in frozen peas and frozen corn.
Remove any skin from the fish. Cut into bite-sized chunks and place into a baking dish. Pour the sauce over the fish. Top with the mashed potatoes, making sure the potatoes reach the edges of the dish in an even layer. Use a fork to give the top texture, and sprinkle grated cheese over the top.
Bake in the oven for about 35 minutes, until the top of the potatoes is golden.

description:

title: The Best "Fog Of War" Puzzle
description:
*** THE SUDOKU EVENT OF THE YEAR: IT'S HERE ***
Huge news:  Phistomefel's first ever sudoku hunt IS OUT!!  We're gifting this to all our patrons to say "Thank you" for supporting us. 

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon has fallen in love with these "fog of war" puzzles and today's - called Fogrotto by Math Pesto - is the best we've seen.  The logic is incredibly interesting and clever from start to finish.  Remember - be careful not to inadvertently enter digits as this could reveal cells behind the fog!

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/77hLMnt2bM

If the fog is absent on your browser you could try the link below:
https://tinyurl.com/2p8uj9ve

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered mostly in darkness. Placing correct digits in cells will illuminate more of the grid. Cells are either wall or cave cells. Walls are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid and the cave is one orthogonally connected area. A 2x2 area cannot be fully wall nor fully cave. White circles are cave cells and the value in a circle is the number of cave cells “seen” in that row and column, including the cell itself. Walls obstruct vision. A cage contains no repeated digits, and the values of the cave cells sum to the given total. Wall cells don’t count towards the sum. (Note: A cage’s clue doesn't necessarily appear in the uppermost nor leftmost cell.) A doubler appears exactly once in each row, column, and 3x3 box. For purposes of circles and cage sums, such cells’ digits are doubled in value. Each digit is doubled once.

title: An Amazing New Rule For Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We only heard about this puzzle this morning but Simon was so impressed with the idea he had to try it immediately.  Indeed none other than Phistomefel wrote "I absolutely love this idea and the puzzle is a beauty!" - enough said!  It's called Deflection and it's by Myxo.

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RJDghqH248

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row, column and box contains exactly one “deflection” cell. Each deflection cell contains a different digit. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along this sum. When a diagonal hits a deflection cell, the diagonal gets deflected clockwise by 90° ("makes a right-turn"). If a diagonal passes the same cell multiple times, that cell's value is counted multiple times towards the clue sum.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
You been asking for Simon to have a go at this one... Chaos CaveSudoku by Magnus Josefsson - one of the most difficult and well-loved sudokus on Logic Masters Germany of recent times.  It is well worth all its plaudits and it is also quite hard... :)

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/49MN7MfH37

Rules: 
Place some digits in the grid and shade some cells so that a) There is a 9x9 subgrid filled with digits that forms a valid standard sudoku; b) disregarding the interior 7x7 of the sudoku subgrid, the rest of the grid forms a valid "cave". A valid Cave is formed where all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected; all shaded cells are orthogonally connected to an edge of the grid (nb the borders around the 7x7 interior of the sudoku are edges for this purpose); each number written in an unshaded cell must show how many cells can be seen from that position horizontally and vertically, where the view is limited by the next shaded cell or an edge of the grid. The cell with the number itself is included in the count; and each number in a shaded cell must equal the total number of cells in that orthogonally connected group of shaded cells.

description:

Another stunning sudoku today - and only slightly easier than yesterday's (!) - it's called Ripple and it's the work of Mormagli.  Basically just three lines for clues but these lines are absolutely magical.

Play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4gn88G8Ftt

Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. title: But - Why aren't there ANY numbers in this sudoku at all?
description:
Here's where you can try X-Sums Killer Sudoku by Udukos: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QMb6m2pdMR 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Numbers outside the grid are X-Sums clues. They indicate the sum of the first X cells in the row/column from that direction, where X is the first number in that row/column. A double-digit X-Sums clue inside a cage prevents BOTH of its digits from appearing anywhere else in the cage (this does mean 11, 22, 33, and 44 are disallowed as X-Sums clues, as those would repeat digits in a cage). A double-digit X-Sums clue may include zero (10, 20, 30, and 40 are valid X-Sums clues).

title: I Told You Not To Do That!!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely stunning debut on the channel today from Al Fresco and their sudoku Double Or Half.  A few weeks ago Simon exclaimed in a video that he didn't want constructors thinking about cells that could halve the value of the digit they contain... well Al Fresco ignored that plea :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/t9R8FpbtRJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages and sum to the cage total. Each row, column and box contains a “doubler” and each row, column and box contains a “halver”. For the purposes of cage totals a digit in a doubler cell counts as twice its face value and a digit in a halver cell counts as half its face value. Each digit 1-9 appears once in a doubler cell and once in a halver cell. Additionally doubler and halver cells cannot be a kings move away from other doubler or halver cells. title: How To Tell If Someone Is Lying
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolute treat today in the form of an approachable "liar" puzzle.  It's called Pinocchio II, it's by thoughtbyte and it's joy to solve from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FpRnpjptb6

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following standard clue types occurs exactly three times in the grid: white dots, black dots, Xs, Vs, German whispers, Grey squares/circles, and cages. For each of those clue types, exactly two of the appearances of that clue are correct, and the other is incorrect. Correct clues would work as follows: A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits; a black dot separates cells containing digits in a 1:2 ratio; cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10; cells separated by a V contain digits summing to 5; adjacent digits along a green “German Whispers” line must differ by at least 5; cells with a grey square must contain an even digit; cells with a grey circle must contain an odd digit; digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage and must not repeat.

description:

We're doing to be trying to Guess The Setter tonight by solving puzzles from the Sudoku Skunkworks. We'd love to have your company if you can join us!

https://youtu.be/yY2VQ263mFE

We've linked two versions:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tgLhMqqHrm

https://tinyurl.com/29ay28tz

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along “renbanmometers”, digits must increase from the bulb end and form a non-repeating consecutive sequence. The renbanmometers in this puzzle are all hidden, only their bulbs and tips are given. Bulbs are larger circles while tips are smaller circles. Corresponding tips and bulbs share the same colour (and letter). Renbanmometers can move diagonally or orthogonally, but renbanmometers cannot ever cross and different renbanmometers cannot share a cell.

title: Only 11 People Have Solved This
description:
*** IF YOU HAVE EVER ENJOYED ONE OF OUR VIDEOS... ***
Then give yourself 17 minutes of joy by watching this video... which features neither Mark nor Simon!

https://youtu.be/FljB9uQ9nFQ

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Not one but two puzzles in tonight's video as Simon attempts Wessel Strijkstra's Never - a sudoku/yajilin hybrid which, we have to say, is just mindblowingly good.  To prepare for the main event, Simon tackles shye's Yajilin from the Discord server Daily Pencil Puzzle channel first :)

Play shye's yajilin here:

https://tinyurl.com/4mnb26sw

Wessel Strijkstra's puzzle can be played here: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JrDMHhgM8Q

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells grey so that no two grey cells are orthogonally adjacent and draw a non-intersecting loop through the centres of all the remaining cells (ie cells that are neither blue nor grey). Blue cells cannot be shaded grey, and digits in blue cells represent the number of grey cells in a straight line in the indicated direction (if given).  All blue cells need arrows and some arrows must be determined by the solver. A clue outside a row gives the sum of the digits on the first horizontal loop segment passing through its row (including the cells in which it turns); likewise for columns and vertical segments.

Shade some cells so that no two shaded cells are orthogonally adjacent and draw a non-intersecting loop through the centers of all the remaining empty cells. Clues cannot be shaded, and represent the number of shaded cells in a straight line in the indicated direction.

title: The Drunkard's Walk
description:
*** My Auntie's Breast Cancer Support Video ***

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=py6rVPtx4hI

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's another Fog Of War sudoku tonight, this time from FullDeck and Missing A Few Cards, our eminent mathematicians from the US!  And it's FullDeck's birthday so many happy returns Eliza - we hope you enjoy Simon's attempt to get to drips with modular lines in the puzzle :)

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://beta.sudokupad.app/Gnb2TrBHnF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. 

After a night of celebrating, our hero leaves r1c1, through the fog, trying to get home to r9c9. With each step, they move to an orthogonally adjacent cell, forming a modular line as they go. (This means that any set of three contiguous cells along their path must include one digit from [147], one digit from [258] and one digit from [369].) 

They stagger from streetlamp (yellow circle) to streetlamp along the way. Some of the streetlamps are visible from the start but others are hidden by the fog and will only be revealed when correct digits are placed nearby. Their path must lead them to every streetlamp. All streetlamps are from the same modular set and, whenever a number from that set is on the path, it appears as a streetlamp. Numbers from that modular set which are not on the path are not streetlamps. 

In cages, digits cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). If our hero enters a cage, they must completely traverse the cage before exiting it. Some killer cages may be avoided entirely.

title: Must A Symmetric Puzzle Have 2 Solutions?
description:
*** IF YOU HAVE EVER ENJOYED ONE OF OUR VIDEOS... ***
Then give yourself 17 minutes of joy by watching this video... which features neither Mark nor Simon!

https://youtu.be/FljB9uQ9nFQ

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
How did we miss this?  It appeared over a year ago and somehow we overlooked solving one of the most brilliant sudokus of all time - yes, it's that good.  Nahileon's 'Symmetry?' exhibits perfect symmetry around its central column and yet it has only one solution.  And this is approachable :) 

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FJf8mBHjH9

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (eg if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same is true of column 5 and the digit 5; and column 9 and the digit 9. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contains digits in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one digit is double the other). Not all possible dots are given. Digits may not repeat on either of the main (blue) diagonals.

title: Oh No! What Has Happened To Simon?
description:
This is where you can try today's Kraken the Kryptic puzzle Subtle Advertisement by Sunnyjum: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gp8DLMT7Qt 

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the arrow’s circle. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase from the bulb. Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the total in the top left corner (if given). Digits separated by an X must sum to 10. Digits along a black line must read the same backwards and forwards. Digits inside a solid grey circle are odd. Check out Can of Wormholes on Steam. Digits along the indicated diagonals must sum to the total given (digits may repeat if allowed by other rules. A number outside the grid without an arrow is an X-Sum clue: the first X digits seen by the clue along its column must sum to the clue’s value, where X is the first digit seen. A clue outside the grid with an arrow shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. The numbers in a white circle must appear in the four cells around that circle. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio with each other. Whew.

Many thanks to Ben Taylor for this wonderful parody video. Mark's video will be coming out 15 minutes later than usual!

title: How Many Wrogns Make A Right?!!
description:
*** KICKSTARTER - JUST 3 DAYS TO GO ***

Brand new stretched goals for the last 3 DAYS:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits-volume-2?ref=4rrd60

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's puzzle is a "wrogn" sudoku in which every rule must be broken in every position it applies!  It's by James Sinclair and it holds the accolade of being the most-solved 100% rated sudoku on Logic Masters Germany.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4JT3tBgh32

Rules: 
[Note we have made a very slight clarification to the rules to make it clear that adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of less than 5.]

Normal sudoku rules apply. ALL clues are wrong. A clue is "wrong" if it is not 100% correct Ie Along purple lines, digits cannot form a consecutive, non-repeating set. Along green lines, at least one pair of adjacent digits must have a difference of less than 5. Along thermometers, digits cannot increase from bulb to tip. (Digits can repeat along purple/green lines and thermometers if allowed by other rules.) Digits on arrows cannot sum to the digit in the attached circle. At least one of the digits inside a (larger) white circle must not appear in any of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in cells separated by a V cannot sum to 5, and digits in cells separated by an X cannot sum to 10. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are not consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot do not have a 1:2 ratio.

*** NEW PATREON SOLVE ***

This is so good that Simon is a tiny bit concerned that it might be enjoyed by a wider audience, despite its ruleset (which is much easier to get to grips with if the solver has a working knowledge of the Japanese logic puzzle Masyu).

title: Simon's Joke ... Becomes My Problem
description:
Sometimes a word spoken in jest develops into a brilliant puzzle. Here's where you can try Don't even think about Halvers! by Andyeka: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8HtThN6DFr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit appearing in a circle must appear in at least one of the cells adjacent to the circle. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). The grid contains 9 "halvers", one in each row, column and 3x3 box. Each digit from 1 to 9 is halved exactly once. A halved digit counts as half its value in a cage sum.

description:

https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2gdj4tn6

https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2p2c9ha3
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first X digits in its row or column, starting with the digit next to the clue (X). (7:00/13:00)

title: The Californian Mountain Snake
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new author makes their debut today, Video Floral, and what a debut.  This is an extraordinary sudoku combining, seemingly effortlessly, normal sudoku, yin-yang, german whispers and renban - all built around this long red snake!  Simon doesn't find this an easy puzzle but boy is it brilliant (and it's got a perfect 100% rating on LMD).

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HQ76Db67Qg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 box may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Along the red line, each run of cells with the same shading contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Along the red line, digits in each pair of adjacent cells with different shading must differ by at least 5. The grey cell is shaded.

title: An Absolutely Incredible Puzzle Combo
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Schrödinger Sodkuro by Ichtues: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qQbmM7j4dM 
Place the digits 0-9 in the grid so that every row, column, and 3x3 box contains every digit exactly once. To enable this, there is a single Schrödinger cell (S-cell) in each row, column and box, containing a superposition of two different digits. Each S-Cell is a Kakuro clue to the right or downwards, showing the sum of digits between that cell and the edge of the grid. A number outside the grid is also a Kakuro clue, showing the sum of digits between the edge of the grid and the next S-clue eg if an S-Cell contains the digits 12, the clue must be twelve or twenty one. Kakuro clues can be zero or have a leading zero. R2c1 contains an even digit.

*** Just a few more days to support the Kickstarter for our second book, Cracking the Cryptic Greatest Hits Volume 2! Check it out here and help us meet more stretch goals to make the book even better: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits-volume-2?ref=4rrd60 ***

title: The Marble Run
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another fantastic sudoku innovation today, this time from ZergreS whose riddle puzzles have featured on the channel many times. The idea is simple - get the marble from the top of the grid to the bottom - but the logic involved is fresh and wonderful.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/r34hQD84Tn

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Find the path of the marble run (from R1C1 to the hole in R9C1). The marble can only drop down or go sideways. It cannot visit a cell more than once. Digits in cages sum to the given total. Cells on the marble's path do not contribute to the sum. No digits can repeat in a cage.

title: A Technical Hitch in the GAS
description:
Here are URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur.

GAS 486 – Quadruples Sudoku by Bill Murphy  https://tinyurl.com/yd7e72n8 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2paapcp3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a white circle appear somewhere in the four cells immediately surrounding that circle (7:00/12:00)

GAS 487 – Gomoku by Philip Newman  https://tinyurl.com/3fyxr2b9 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2pf9nr29
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set in any order.  (7:56/14:32)

GAS 488 – Sum or Greater by Clover https://tinyurl.com/mjr838js
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2e6an7e4
Normal sudoku rules apply. The value in a circle tells you either the sum of the digits or the greater of the two values in the cells it appears between. (8:00/15:00)

GAS 489 – Dot.Com Sudoku by Bill Murphy  https://tinyurl.com/2px3ujhs
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2mg5ne9l
Normal sudoku rules apply. A plus sign on the intersection of four cells indicates that both pairs of diagonally opposite pairs of digits have the same sum. A minus sign indicates that both pairs have the same difference. Not all pluses or minuses are given. (06:39/10:32)

GAS 490 – Cereal Convention Sudoku by Philip
https://tinyurl.com/scw2c723  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2eanrh5e
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the total given. Digits along a line have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line. (10:00/18:00)

title: Which Solver Will You Watch?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's puzzle is a belter from AnalyticalNinja and combines sudoku with fillomino in a highly entertaining and interesting way.  The only downside is that the sudoku (which is 100% rated) is quite tricky - which has necessitated a movie length video!  And there are other solvers in movies on TV at the moment so we worry you won't watch us... Do you prefer Enola, Sherlock or Simon?!  So that's Millie Bobby Brown, Henry Cavill or... Simon.  Hmmm.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mGtft8fRN9

Rules: 
Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column, 3x3 box, or coloured region. Divide the grid into coloured regions so that no two coloured regions of the same size (ie containing the same number of cells) shares an edge. Numbers that match a coloured region’s size CANNOT be placed into the cells in that region. Eg a coloured region of size 3 cannot contain any 3s within it. The small clue in the top left corner of a cage indicates both the total size in cells of any coloured regions that overlap the cage, as well as the sum of the digits within that cage. Digits can't repeat within a cage. The indicated diagonals show both the total size in cells of any coloured regions that overlap the cells on that diagonal, as well as the sum of the digits along that diagonal. Eg a diagonal clue of 7 would indicate that the digits in/along it would either come from the same 7 cell coloured region, or multiple coloured regions whose total size equals 7.

title: Which Way in the Fog?
description:
Here's where you can try Go the Right Way by Panthera: https://tinyurl.com/5xvnzfv6  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some Japanese sums rules apply: There is a 6x6 grid in boxes 5/6/8/9. Blue cells in boxes 2/3/4/7 act as Japanese sum clues for this 6x6 grid, giving the sum of contiguous runs of blue-shaded cells within the grid. Two-digit clues are read top-to-bottom or left-to-right. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of the same color. A black dot separates digits with a 1 to 2 ratio. A white dot separates digits with a difference of 1 (or the given number when given). Not all dots are given. Fog rules apply. The fog will clear as you place digits correctly.

However, digits may be repeated within a row. One of the columns is magic. Each digit in the magic column tells you how many times that digit appears in its row. Eg: the 3 in the magic column has exactly three 3s in its row (including itself.) Digits along a thin blue line always add up to 10. Blue lines never pass through any empty cells.

description:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy Halloween!  To celebrate, we're taking a look at Math Pesto's puzzle based on the classic 1982 John Carpenter film The Thing!  This is SUCH a good sudoku - an absolute treat from start to finish.  Flame-throwers ready?  

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/mr3m8d8p

For those of you who struggle with tinyurl links, here is a link to our software:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FrQ76Q9jmD

Rules: 
100,000 years ago, a UFO crash landed in Antarctica. Norwegian researchers discovered the site in 1982 and, having brought a frozen passenger from that UFO back to their lab, accidentally revived it. The Thing murdered a crew member and then assimilated him in order to kill off the others. It has now imitated one of their dogs and is making its way to Outpost #31, where a U.S. crew might meet the same fate…

Normal sudoku rules apply. Once in each row, column, and box, the Thing assimilates a number, thereby negating it (e.g. if the Thing is in R5C7 and the cell appears to contain a 3, its actual value is –3). Values on the blue line have the same sum in each 3x3 box the line is in. Values along a thermo increase from the bulb end. Adjacent values on a green line differ by 5 or more. Numbers in a circle appear once in the four surrounding cells; they may be genuine (positive) or they may be the Thing (negative). To successfully escape, you must travel from the now destroyed Outpost #31 (R2C2) to the helicopter (R8C8). Your path is one cell wide and may not go outside of Antarctica's boundary (blue line). The path which travels orthogonally may not contain nor be orthogonally adjacent to any of the Thing's cells. Adjacent values on the escape route differ by 5 or more.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the corresponding circle. Adjacent digits on a green whisper line must have a difference of at least 5.

GTS 5 Killer Sudoku by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9rbTF4thGQ 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages cannot contain repeat digits and show their sums.

GTS 6 LK-Sandwich by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HPpFF7gRBn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid with an arrow shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. A clue outside the grid with no arrow shows the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.

GTS 8 AntiKnight, AntiKing Killer by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bJM9GDhF6R 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight’s move or a king’s move apart. The digits inside a cage sum to the total indicated on the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat inside cages. The killer cages themselves must be deduced and drawn by the solver. The cage can have any length and shape. Cages may not overlap. The squares in the grid show where the total of the cages are. The killer cage total must always be at the upper left corner (topmost prioritized over leftmost).

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pM7jd2QbmD

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells marked with a circle contain an odd digit; cells marked with a square contain an even digit. Two neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. You must put this pattern of clues into the grid 7 times:
□ ⟋ □
⟋ 5 ○
□ ○ ○
The patterns may overlap with each other or the given clues. If there is an overlap all clues must still be valid. Digits may repeat within a pattern. You may not rotate or mirror the pattern or put it partially off the grid.

Jay Dyer has a reputation for genius and her puzzle Double The Heat has barely been solved at all...  The reason, it turns out, is because it is COMPLETELY MAD (and bafflingly brilliant).  One of the hardest and most wonderful sudokus we have ever seen. TAKE A BOW!

title: Crazy Shapes - Slotted into Place
description:
Here's where you can try Pentomino Sight Lines by Blobz: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gJBh3q6mmr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; not all such dots are shown. The indicated 60-cell white region contains one each of the twelve standard pentominoes. Each pentomino contains exactly one given digit. That digit indicates the number of cells of the pentomino that are 'seen' orthogonally from that position (including itself). Once placed, each pentomino behaves like a 5-cell killer cage: digits do not repeat and must sum to the value listed below (using standard pentomino labeling):
F=30, I=26, L=24, N=17, P=33, T=17, U=15, V=25, W=26, X=25, Y=23, Z=31
Illustrated Pentominoes at: https://tinyurl.com/pent-labels

title: The Messier Galaxies
description:
*** IT'S LIVE: OUR KICKSTARTER CAMPAIGN LAUNCHED ***
Thank you so much to everyone who supported our Kickstarter which launched last Wednesday.  Want to take a grab a copy of Cracking The Cryptic's Greatest Hit Volume 2?  Here's the link:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

When the mighty constructor Qodec recommends a puzzle to us, we listen!  Today Simon attempts an exceptionally beautiful and cunning sudoku called Messier 43 by Memeristor.  This is magical - one might even say stellar :)
 
Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/ThQmPfrLmT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  The dots given in the grid are the centres of (rotationally) symmetric "galaxies" (non-overlapping sets of orthogonally-connected cells), which function as "Region Sum Areas".  Cells in Region Sum Areas have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box they visit, and they must visit more than one 3x3 box.  Not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy. eg if a galaxy consisted of r6c6, r5c6, r5c7, r4c7, r4c8 and r3c8 then r6c6+r5c6 [box 5] = r5c7+r4c7+r4c8 [box 6] = r3c8 [box3].

title: The Future Of Sudoku
description:
*** IT'S LIVE: OUR KICKSTARTER CAMPAIGN LAUNCHED ***
Thank you so much to everyone who supported our Kickstarter which launched last Wednesday.  Want to take a grab a copy of Cracking The Cryptic's Greatest Hit Volume 2?  Here's the link:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits-volume-2?ref=4rrd60

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

We have seen the future of sudoku.  Innovation drips from Chameleon's latest puzzle.  You only get 5 lives to solve it (!) and the digits you manage to deduce REVEAL more of the puzzle.  This is quite simply magnificent.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://yusitnikov.github.io/puzzletv/#lumos-maxima

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Each circle occupies a single cell (so no double-digit arrow totals are possible). In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The grid is covered with fog. There are two initial light sources that illuminate the darkness and clear the fog. Put correct digits into the cells to get more light (it's ok to put a digit into a cell that is covered by fog). You have 5 lives to solve the puzzle. It costs 1 life for each wrong digit entered. Note: no guessing is required to finish the puzzle. The extra lives are given only to allow for possible typos.

[NB If you do use all your lives, the puzzle will freeze and you will have to start again so it is very important to enter digits carefully.]

https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2qtzk476 (8:00/15:00)

Here's where you can play Ludoku by questionable_compensation: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/76q9qg3JDg 
Normal sudoku rules apply. On green lines, adjacent digits differ by at least 5. Digits on the blue line must lie between the digits placed on either end of the line. On the red line, each set of 3 adjacent digits contains 1 number from each of the sets: (1,4,7) (2,5,8) (3,6,9). On the yellow line, each set of 3 adjacent digits contains 1 number from each of the sets: (1,2,3) (4,5,6) (7,8,9). The digit in a white circle must be in one of the cells connected to that circle. 
The central 'minimum' digit is smaller than its 4 orthogonally adjacent digits.

title: A Quick GAS Top-Up
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles. Hat times are given as (two hats/one hat). Any correct solution gets you a dinosaur.
GAS 461 – Countdown Killer Sudoku by Philip https://tinyurl.com/255ez3rw
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2fusp822 (6:00/12:00)
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal sum to 14 and may repeat if allowed by other rules.

GAS 462 – Count the Odd Ones Sudoku by Clover  https://tinyurl.com/5t2f3bwh 
 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2mw45xql (8:00/15:00)
Normal sudoku rules. If a digit appears in a circle, it tells you the total number of odd digits along the attached line (not including the digit in the circle itself, which may be odd or even.) 

GAS 463 – Extra Regions Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes. https://tinyurl.com/2p85h2ux  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2pxhptth (6:30/12:00)
Normal Sudoku rules. Each grey region also contains every digit exactly once.

GAS 464 – Summetry by Philip Newman https://tinyurl.com/yc36n8fv
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2k5wlpat (7:00/13:00)
Normal sudoku rules. For each marked line, the digits in every region it passes through have the same sum.  

GAS 465 – Entropy Sudoku by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/hp9tyrb3 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2fkvlvl3 (6:00/11:00)
Normal sudoku rules. Each 2x2 square of cells must contain at least one low digit (123), at least one medium digit (456), and at least one high digit (789).

title: Can You Solve The Impossible Sudoku?
description:
*** KICKSTARTER LAUNCHING WEDNESDAY 8.30PM UK TIME ***
We're planning a Kickstarter campaign to help the creation of our new book: Cracking The Cryptic's Greatest Hit Volume 2.  It should go live at 8.30pm TOMORROW!

Here's the link for anyone interested in helping make it happen:

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits-volume-2

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy Birthday RockyRoer!  Simon attempts RockyRoer's astonishing What Do Killers Eat? sudoku - a puzzle with a remarkable lack of digits.  This one is absolutely stunning though so do give it a go if you can!

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hJLgmn2GfH

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits cannot repeat. The digits in each cage sum to the “cage total”. Clues outside of the grid (“Sandwich totals”) are the sum of the digits between the 1 and 9 in their row/column. In every row and column containing a “?”, the sandwich total will be equal to one of the cage totals in that row/column. Nothing is known about rows/columns with no ? clue. EG Row 7's sandwich total is either equal to the cage total from column 1's 7-cell cage, the 8-cell L shaped cage in column 2, the 4 cell cage in column 3, the 2 cell cage in Box 8, the 5 cell cage in boxes 5/8, or the 9 cell cage in boxes 8 and 9.

description:
The Guess the Setter puzzles:

GTS 2 8x8 Irregular Renban AntiXV by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fmt4P39DJt 
1-8 must be placed in each row, column and marked region. A purple line contains a sequence of consecutive digits in any order. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Cells separated by a V sum to 5. All X's and V's are given.

GTS 3 Palindrome Killer Arrow by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nqJT7rmmQL 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line is a palindrome, reading the same in both directions. Cages show their sums. Digits on an arrow sum to the number in the circle.

GTS 4 Arrow Whispers Sudoku by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jgJMLmBqQt 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the corresponding circle. Adjacent digits on a green whisper line must have a difference of at least 5.

GTS 5 Killer Sudoku by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9rbTF4thGQ 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages cannot contain repeat digits and show their sums.

GTS 6 LK-Sandwich by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HPpFF7gRBn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid with an arrow shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. A clue outside the grid with no arrow shows the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.

GTS 8 AntiKnight, AntiKing Killer by ???: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bJM9GDhF6R 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight’s move or a king’s move apart. The digits inside a cage sum to the total indicated on the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat inside cages. The killer cages themselves must be deduced and drawn by the solver. The cage can have any length and shape. Cages may not overlap. The squares in the grid show where the total of the cages are. The killer cage total must always be at the upper left corner (topmost prioritized over leftmost).

Normal sudoku rules apply. Along lines, the region sums form a consecutive ordered sequence. We're going to stream tonight at 10pm UK time. Please note that right at the end of the solve, Simon makes a "deliberate mistake" (Simon's words) for the eagle-eyed among you to spot.  It doesn't change any of the logic but it does mean the final grid is very slightly INCORRECT!  Can you spot Simon's error?

Normal sudoku rules apply. In graves (cages), digits must sum to the day, month or year of the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. title: The 11x11 NOT Sudoku
description:
*** OCTOBER MONTHLY REWARD - OUT NOW ***

The Duality Sudoku Hunt is just out.  Massive thanks and kudos to the Sudoku Skunkworks for creating such a brilliant set of puzzles (14 in all!).  You'll be able to enter the competition if you can solve the first 4 sudokus.  If you solve all 14, you'll get a shoutout.

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LLTqgTJ682

Join us on Patreon to watch the video for as little as $2/month here:  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

This 11x11 grid has certain sudoku elements but it's got more in common with the Japanese logic puzzle Nurikabe.  What we can tell you is that Polynesia by Agent is just about the perfect puzzle.  It's also not THAT hard.  Just read the rules a couple of times before you attempt it :)

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qp37n87R4b

Rules: 
Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area can be fully shaded. Place some digits from 1 to 9 in unshaded cells such that no repeating digits occur in any row or column. Shaded cells do not contain digits. Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands, which do not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. An island of size N must contain the digits 1 to N once each. Cells with arrows contain a digit that indicates the total number of unshaded cells (including itself) in the indicated directions combined. Caged cells contain a digit that indicates the size of the corresponding island. All possible cages are given.

title: Y Is This Puzzle So Brilliant?
description:
*** OCTOBER MONTHLY REWARD - OUT NOW ***

The Duality Sudoku Hunt is just out.  Massive thanks and kudos to the Sudoku Skunkworks for creating such a brilliant set of puzzles (14 in all!).  You'll be able to enter the competition if you can solve the first 4 sudokus.  If you solve all 14, you'll get a shoutout.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

It's always a good day when there's a new Phistomefel sudoku to solve!  It's called Sum Line Sudoku #1 and it's a constraint we haven't seen before. The logic is gorgeous, you won't want to miss this one.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GJ9PTHm8N7

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie fill the grid with the numbers from 1 to 9 so that in each row, column, and 3x3 block, each digit occurs exactly once). For every triple of adjacent digits on a line, one of the digits has to be the sum of the other two, e.g. 2-5-7, 6-9-3, and 8-4-4 are valid adjacent digits along a line. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by the other rules. NB Each line in the shape of a Y consists of three lines, each of three cells length. For instance, the line running in boxes 1 and 4 contains the three lines R2C2-R3C2-R4C1, R2C2-R3C2-R4C3, and R4C1-R3C2-R4C3.

description:
*** OCTOBER MONTHLY REWARD - OUT NOW ***

The Duality Sudoku Hunt was released yesterday.  Massive thanks and kudos to the Sudoku Skunkworks for creating such a brilliant set of puzzles (14 in all).  You'll be able to enter the competition if you can solve the first 4 sudokus.  If you solve all 14, you'll get a shoutout.

Join us on Patreon to watch the video for as little as $2/month here:  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Mark sends Simon through another of his prank sudokus today with Chameleon's Quantum-safe Sudoku.  This is absolutely bonkers.  The idea is that you cannot solve it (!) but figuring out how to not solve it is... quite hard!!!  

Play this extraordinary "sudoku" at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pntP7GhPHF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one digit must be double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  Not all possible dots are given. Cages are “Schrödinger cells” ie they contain one of 2 values. After filling all regular cells with digits, all Schrödinger cells must remain unresolved (in other words, both values of every Schrödinger cell must allow for a valid sudoku solution). The quantum balance of the universe is safe with this sudoku. Cats are safe too.

[Note there is a tiny change to the rules above vs those which Simon faced in the video. We used "allow for" rather than "lead to".  We do not think this will affect anyone's solve at all but we just thought it might clarify one tiny aspect of the puzzle.]

title: A Sudoku Can't Have Negative Numbers... Can It?!
description:
*** OCTOBER MONTHLY REWARD - OUT NOW ***

The Duality Sudoku Hunt was released today.  Massive thanks and kudos to the Sudoku Skunkworks for creating such a brilliant set of puzzles (14 in all!).  You'll be able to enter the competition if you can solve the first 4 sudokus.  If you solve all 14, you'll get a shoutout.

We've also just released Simon & Mark's solve of Vignettes by zetamath, which you can play at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LLTqgTJ682

Join us on Patreon to watch the video for as little as $2/month here:  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

We've been entertained with "doubler" cells in recent weeks but the_cogito wasn't satisfied with that and he's invented the concept of "negators" - cells that count as their negative value!!  The highest praise we can give this sudoku is that it is (positively!) Phistomefelian.  

Play "Broken Pencil" by the_cogito at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/R2hQpqmG63

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a blue line must have an equal sum within each 3x3 box the line passes through. (Eg r9c7 = r9c6 + r8c5 + r9c4).  However every row, column, and 3x3 box contains exactly one “negator cell”. The digit in a negator cell acts as the negative of its value for the purpose of any line that passes through it (eg, a 4 in a negator cell would instead act as -4). The location of these cells must be determined. Digits in negator cells must contain all the digits 1-9 once each.

title: It's All Gone WROGN - AGAIN!!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

[Apologies for the length of this video.  It is always difficult to judge just how hard 5* puzzles might prove to be!] 

In December 2020, Simon attempted a puzzle called Everything Is Wrogn by DiMono... a puzzle in which all the usual rules of sudoku were broken...  Today Simon attempts the sequel.  And, yes, rest assured, everything is still absolutely WROGN with this one!  This is a brilliant and brutal sudoku so do allow yourself plenty of time if you want to get it finished :)

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/944Mg3fnJH

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply (yay!). Digits along a purple or red “renban” line MUST ALL repeat, and MAY NOT be chosen from consecutive digits (i.e. 445577 is valid but 445566 is not). Digits along a grey palindrome line MUST NOT read the same in both directions. Digits along a thermometer MUST NOT increase from the bulb end. Digits along the negative diagonal (marked in blue) MUST ALL repeat. Diagonals indicated by arrows outside the grid MUST NOT sum to the indicated value. Clues outside the grid MUST NOT be valid X-Sum or Skyscraper clues, as defined below. In a valid X-Sum clue, the first X digits seen by the clue, where X is the first seen digit, sum to the number in the clue (i.e. 382xxxxxx would be a 13 clue). In a valid Skyscraper clue, consider the digits as heights of buildings, where taller buildings hide smaller buildings behind them. The clue outside the grid indicates how many buildings can be "seen" from the clue (i.e. 462187593 would be a 4 from the left (4 → 6 → 8 → 9) and a 2 from the right (3 → 9).

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Who better to continue a week of absolutely incredible puzzles than Jay Dyer - a setter who seems to only make 100%-rated sudokus.  This one is called Overkill and features "doublers"!

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qbGThhnqM9

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat, and sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Nine cells (one in each row/column/3x3 box) are "doublers", and count as double their value in cage sums. Each digit appears in exactly one doubler. Doublers are not necessarily in cages.

title: Sudoku on Steroids
description:
Here's where you can try Kropki on Steroids Sudoku by MarcinJ: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Pd2RLT7dpm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a larger blue line have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box it passes through. Digits cannot repeat on the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a black dot (either diagonally or orthogonally) have a 1:2 ratio, e.g. R1C2 and R2C3 have a 1:2 ratio, and so do R2C2 and R1C3. Digits separated by a white dot (either diagonally or orthogonally) are consecutive, e.g. R1C7 and R6C8 are consecutive, and so are R6C7 and R5C8. Not all possible dots are given.

title: When Knight's Moves Don't Lead To Resignation :)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

It was going to be a tough task to follow the week of puzzles that we've just showcased but Adem Jaziri has done just that with this sublime sudoku called The Ls.  This is definitely approachable (and wonderful)!  

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FF8fN88npr

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, which can appear in any order.

title: GAS Gets Creative
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku puzzles):
GAS 441 – Up and Down Sudoku by Sam https://tinyurl.com/4f4m6vrk 
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2zsdp28g
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each grey line, digits alternately increase and decrease.
GAS 442 – Vi Veri Vsvdokvm Vivvs Vici by Philip https://tinyurl.com/msbupcuy
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2fb6n7vh
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a V must sum to 5.
GAS 443 – Word Search Sudoku by clover. https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7b2PqqDQmh https://tinyurl.com/2qmoyotg
Normal sudoku rules apply, except that the puzzle uses the letters BESOLVING rather than the digits 1 through 9. Also, the words from the word bank must each appear along one of the heavy gray lines. A word appears in order along its line, but it may start on either end of the line. 
GAS 444 – X-Sums Sudoku by Sam https://tinyurl.com/m8swrasp
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2oascawq
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the nearest X numbers in the corresponding row or column, where X is the first of those numbers. For example, a clue of 12 could be satisfied by, for example, 4512 (where X is 4), or 327 (where X is 3).
GAS 445 – Yippee Ki Yay, Y'all by Philip https://tinyurl.com/2p94fndu
https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2po5fa8n
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Within cages digits cannot repeat, and must increase from left to right (in rows) and top to bottom (in columns).

title: This CANNOT Exist... (And Yet It Does)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

[Simon writes] I'm pretty sure now that this was a prank by Mark and that he didn't think I'd actually try this puzzle once I saw what it was...  it's called Self-determination and it's the (unbelievable) work of Stephane Bura.  It is the most daunting ruleset/grid combo I think we've ever seen.  Good luck!!

Please do leave a comment if you enjoy this video - in our opinion, Stephane deserves all the plaudits in the world for somehow creating this one.

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8L2Pmn44rp

Rules: 
Place the digits 1 to 8 in each row and each column.  Each horizontal domino that has both its digits in the first 7 columns forms the coordinates of a digit in the grid:  The leftmost member of the pair is its row. The rightmost member of the pair is its column. Its value is the row in which the pair is. For instance, if R4C1 contains 7 and R4C2 contains 5 then R7C5 contains 4.

More examples of how the rules work can be found here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000B3Z

title: The 8x8 Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

These halcyon days for variant sudokus continue with a 100% rated "easy" puzzle from Jakhob and wooferzfg called Pieces.  Like yesterday, this seems to require some slightly different ways of thinking and we love it!!!
You can try it at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/y44rf3fp

If you cannot use tinyurl links then use:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3r8FmBhLH2

Rules: 
In each of the 4x4 grids, place exactly 4 of the digits from 1 to 9, such that digits do not repeat in the 2x2 regions. Digits may not repeat in a row or column of the full 8x8 grid. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive and non-repeating digits, in any order. Digits on arrows must sum to the digit in the circle. Neighboring digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. In cages, digits must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.

title: "I'm Blown Away"
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

What an extraordinary time this is for variant sudokus.  The last few days have featured exceptional puzzles and now here is yet another: Magnus Josefsson's Chaos FilloSudokumino has been praised to the nines by the community and now we get to solve it.  It's weird but it's utterly wonderful.

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/889gtdBFbB

Rules: 
Place a number in every cell of the grid such that: 1. There is a 9x9 subgrid that forms a valid standard sudoku; and 2. Disregarding the interior 7x7 area of the sudoku subgrid, the rest of the grid (including the 1-cell wide perimeter of the sudoku grid) forms a valid fillomino.  [Standard fillomino rules are as follows: a) Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells and enter into each cell the size of its region; b) No two regions of the same size may share an edge.

An example puzzle can be seen here:

title: Can You Deduce The Chess Position?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Yesterday we featured on the most amazing sudokus we've ever seen (Dragonsnake by Agent) and today we get to do it all again.  This is an extraordinary hybrid puzzle of sudoku and chess where the solver's task is to deduce the current state of a chess game and, in doing so, solve the sudoku.  It's by Christian König and it's called Ein Echtes Schachsudoku.  [You will need to know the rules of chess to solve this puzzle!]

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jMQR24JRBN

Rules: 
Right now we are in the middle of a game of chess. There have been some moves made by standard chess rules, but neither a capture nor a castling have yet taken place. Also, every piece has been moved at most once. Every piece carries a digit from 1 to 8 as shown in the initial grid - this digit must appear in the current cell of the piece in the game we're part way through. In the current game position, the whole grid can be filled with digits from 1 to 8, such that every digit appears in every row, column and box exactly once! Can you discover the current chess position and solve the sudoku?

Here is where you can try Six by Tidepoolsalts: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/PFr2r23jL3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are 13 hexomino regions throughout the white cells in the puzzle. Digits cannot repeat within a hexomino, and each hexomino must be different. Small white dots indicate that two cells are in separate hexominoes, and that the difference between them is 1. Small black dots indicate that two cells are in the same hexomino, and that the ratio between them is 2. Large white dots indicate that exactly three of the four cells surrounding them are in the same hexomino. When these large white dots have numbers inside these numbers must be in the cells immediately surrounding them. Large black dots indicate that all four of the cells surrounding them are in the same hexomino.

And here is where you can revisit Bis Repetita by Zelbulon: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4hmqJ9MJF2

title: The GAS Gets Away
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 431 – Killer! By clover https://tinyurl.com/4v4e3t6f https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2qbf6s6z
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given.
GAS 432 – Lockout Lines by Sam https://tinyurl.com/3bymupyd https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2h3kjmdg
Normal Sudoku rules apply. If two diamonds are directly connected by a line, then the numbers in the diamonds must differ by at least 4, and the numbers on the line must NOT be between the numbers in the diamonds.
GAS 433 – Meanie, Miny, Moe by Philip https://tinyurl.com/yscpfaut https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2jml3fs2
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a green square have an arithmetic mean of 5. Digits in cells separated by a blue circle have an arithmetic mean less than 5. Digits in cells separated by a pink (non-square) rectangle have an arithmetic mean greater than 5. (E.g., the arithmetic mean of 3 and 6 is (3+6)/2 = 4.5)
GAS 434 – Nonconsec by clover https://tinyurl.com/yckuxedn https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2jflwvny
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in orthogonally adjacent cells (sharing an edge) may not be consecutive.
GAS 435 – Odd by Sam https://tinyurl.com/4rrwauvw https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2gdjo66q
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits in grey circles are odd.

description:
*** WE ARE STREAMING TONIGHT ***

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mJ3HbD6n9p

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade a single group of orthogonally connected cells in each dashed cage. Shaded groups may not share a dashed border. Each cage must contain at least one shaded cell, and two cages which share a border cannot contain the same number of shaded cells. Digits MAY REPEAT in cages. Some cages have one or two sums indicated. The first value given is the sum of all digits in shaded cells in that cage and, if given, the second is the sum of all digits in unshaded cells in the cage. A cage sum given as "X" is to be determined by the solver and is the same value in all appearances.

NB We have slightly amended the rules above from those which appear in the video to make it clearer that no two cages that share a border can have equal numbers of shaded cells.

What can we say that does today's puzzle justice?  Perhaps we should leave it to two esteemed solvers: Emre Kolotoglu (kolot) and TotallyNormalCat - both of whom rate this as one of the best sudokus of all time. It's called Four Colour Theorem and it's another work of genius from Jay Dyer.  Be ready for your head to get scrambled (unless you've got a more sensible head than Simon)!

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6j3GrPqpDb

Rules: 
Each row, column, and 9-cell region must contain the digits 1-9 once each. The regions must be determined by the solver. Each region must be coloured in its entirety with a single colour. No two regions of the same colour may share an edge, and at most four distinct colours may be used. Cells containing arrows give the distance to the nearest cell of the same colour in each indicated direction (neighbouring cells are a distance 1 from each other). All possible arrows are given.

description:
*** STOP PRESS: BUY OUR BOOK WITH A SPECIAL DISCOUNT + NEW FREE APP ***

To celebrate achieving 500k subscribers, we're trying to say thank you in a couple of ways. We're able to offer our Cracking The Cryptic Greatest Hits book at a discount for a limited period.

We've also just released a free app full of handmade puzzles to celebrate reaching 500,000 subscribers on YouTube. Simply download the (free) Cracking The Cryptic app on Android, Steam or App Store and then select the 500k pack. Enjoy! 

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

A celebration of Star Trek today from filuta and Nordy and their puzzle Where No Snake Has Gone Before.  This is such an excellent sudoku, blending originality, thematic content and an amazing logical journey that remains rich right to the end.  LIVE LONG & PROSPER.

You can try it at the link below: 

Intergalactic-graphics version (as Simon solves in the video):
https://tinyurl.com/yj5k8zt3

Normal version:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TbQfBD6j8j

NB Both puzzles are the same; one just looks more Trekky!

Rules: 
This puzzle is an 11x11 grid with a normal 9x9 Sudoku centered inside. Within the 9x9 Sudoku grid, normal sudoku rules apply: place the digits 1 to 9 in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Draw a snake (non-looping, non-branching 1-cell wide path of orthogonally connected cells) that may touch itself diagonally but not orthogonally. The two ends of the snake are given as large white circles (UFOs). Within the 9x9 Sudoku, all of the odd digits (and none of the even digits) belong to the snake. The snake may appear in any cell within the 11x11 grid, and may move in and out of the 9x9 Sudoku as necessary. Cells outside the 9x9 Sudoku have no numerical value—they exist only for the snake. Digits separated by a white dot (sun) must be consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot (moon) must have a ratio of 2:1. Not all dots are given.

There is an example puzzle available at:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000AG5

title: GAS with Abnormal Rules
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku puzzles):
GAS 426 – Fortress Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p9xtt2e  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2xq6re7e 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Wherever a shaded cell and an unshaded cell are adjacent, the number in the shaded cell must be higher. 
GAS 427 – Germaine Gossip by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2smu9bua https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2j5odexj  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells directly connected by a green line must differ by at least 5.
GAS 428 – Hexagonal Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2q6dg4a3 
Normal sudoku rules DO NOT apply. Instead, fill the grid with the digits 1 through 7, so that each digit appears exactly once in each of the seven bold-outlined regions. Digits that see each other (horizontally or along either diagonal) may not repeat (see attached image, which shows example 'rows' and 'columns'). 
GAS 429 – Irregular Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/56ua4438 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2eqr9brs 
Normal sudoku rules DO NOT apply. Place a number from 1-9 into each empty cell so that every row, column and region contains each number exactly once.
GAS 430 – Jocular Jaunt by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2zz24c3v https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2osx9kxt 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that the clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs of shaded cells found in that row or column. Multiple runs in the same row or column must be separated by at least one unshaded cell.

description:

We've also just released a free app full of handmade puzzles to celebrate reaching 500,000 subscribers on YouTube. Simply download the (free) Cracking The Cryptic app on Android, Steam or App Store and then select the 500k pack. Enjoy! 

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

A brand new one today from the ever-popular Peter Veenis, who has combined one of Simon's favourite logic puzzles (Nurikabe) with sudoku.  We're not sure how hard this one but we do know it's brilliant and it's called Dodekanesos.

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MRfqQRbHmB

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the grid according to the following rules: all odd digits are 'water' and should be unshaded; all even digits must be shaded to form islands; all water cells must be orthogonally connected but there cannot be any 2x2 areas of water. An island is formed of orthogonally connected cells. Islands cannot touch each other orthogonally but they can touch diagonally. Digits may repeat on an island. A cage cell is representing the leftmost cell in the top row of an island and the clue of the cage cell is equal to the sum of digits of the island. Not necessarily all cage cells are given.

description:
*** STOP PRESS: BUY OUR BOOK WITH A SPECIAL DISCOUNT + NEW FREE APP ***

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Today's sudoku has been recommended to us by some wonderful setters, including Dying Flutchman.  It's called Yin Yang Vaults by Schwupel.  However...  Simon had a reunion today with an old school friend and seems to have consumed rather too much wine.  This may (or may not) have impeded his solving - you will have to tell us!!!

You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/brQJjfHMDb

Rules: 
Place the digits 1 to 9 once each into every row, column and 3x3 box. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are connected orthogonally and all unshaded cells are connected orthogonally. No 2x2 box may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first continuous block of shaded cells seen from that direction. Blue cages are "vaults". Digits MAY repeat within a vault. Any digit within a vault must not appear in any cells orthogonally adjacent to that vault. The largest digit in any given vault is equal to the number of shaded cells inside that vault.

description:
*** STOP PRESS: BUY OUR BOOK WITH A SPECIAL DISCOUNT ***

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

We need to start with an apology to constructor Jeff Wajes, who created the extraordinary puzzle Simon attempts in this evening's video.  It's called Odd Pentominoes On The Loose and it takes Simon a VERY long time.  Having finished recording the video, we received a (CRUEL) email from our tester apologising for missing a CLUE in the version Simon was sent. (Simon should have been given an additional X between r4c4 and r5c4.)

We think the video is still worth showing because the puzzle is that good and (we think) a lot of Jeff's intended logic survives the missing X.  

If you decide to attempt the puzzle, our strong recommendation is that you try the puzzle with the correct clues (using the first link below) but, if you really want an even harder challenge, then the second link is to the version Simon tries in the video.

Link 1 (the correct puzzle): 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tbdnBm9fJp

Link 2 (the version attempted by Simon in the video):
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mmqTRbDR68

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A pentomino is a set of 5 orthogonally connected cells. There are exactly 12 different possible pentomino shapes (treating reflections/rotations as equivalent). Arrange all 12 pentominoes in the grid so that 9 of them contain only odd digits. Digits CAN repeat inside a pentomino. Pairs of cells connected by an X or V sum to 10 or 5 respectively AND belong to two separate pentominoes. Not every X and V is given. Along the thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end.

title: What is an Ambiguous Clue?
description:
Here's where you can play City Planning by Auul: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/th7jjqF7hL 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are either skyscraper clues or self-numbered rooms. There is exactly one of each for each digit 1-9. Skyscraper clues represent the number of digits 'visible' along the row or column. Higher digits obscure lower ones, so only digits higher than any previous digit encountered are 'visible'. Self-numbered room clues indicate both the location of a digit N cells away from the edge along the given row or column, and the digit N which will be found in that cell. For example, a self-numbered 4 indicates that the 4th cell away from the edge will contain a 4.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat. In each of the nine 3x3 regions of the grid, there is exactly one killer cage that is 'lying': the small number provided is NOT the correct sum of the digits in that cage. All other cages give the correct sum of their digits.
GAS 417 – XV Quads by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/muvm8mrw https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2a4yqxlx 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two cells are separated by an X or a V then the numbers they contain must add up to 10 or 5 respectively. Numbers in a white circle must appear somewhere in the four cells around the circle.
GAS 418 – I’m a Man, I’m 40 by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/yckwcmxm https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2dp6vlbj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase from bulb to tip.
GAS 419 – Extra Regions by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/rdhjmp5j https://f-puzzles.com/?id=25zcwclq 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each shaded gray region contains the digits 1 through 9 once each.

description:

On the 5th anniversary of the first time we did a sudoku on the channel, we're delighted to attempt this 100% rated puzzle by Agent called Antithesis... But wait - why do some of the cages have negative totals?!!

Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bm7dTjjBRb

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are connected orthogonally and all unshaded cells are connected orthogonally. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. However, shaded cells are treated as negative. In other words, the cage total is the sum of unshaded cells minus the sum of shaded cells.

Numbers in the grid represent the heights of skyscrapers, and clues outside the grid indicate the number of skyscrapers visible in that row or column, looking in that direction. title: Snakes Always Have Chaotic Energy
description:
Here's where you can try Pierced Snake by AndreasV: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tGf29NLMRT 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the number in the circle. There is one 1-cell-wide snake (with a head and a tail) that enters each box exactly once. It may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The number in any circle indicates how many cells the snake occupies in that box. The first two digits on the arrow, as read from the circle, give a 2-digit number showing the sum of the snake's cells in the circle's box.

title: Going Full GAS
description:
Here are the URL's (2 each) for today's 5 puzzles:
GAS 406 – Connect the Dots by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/4udnfdk5  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=226xnxuy 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive (have a difference of 1); digits in cells separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. (No negative constraint - other pairs of digits may also be consecutive or have a 2:1 ratio.)
GAS 407 – First Impression by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/mr2jc29d https://f-puzzles.com/?id=24o68m6o 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in gray squares must be greater than both the first digit in their row and the first digit in their column. For instance, if the gray square in r4c2 contains a 6, then r4c1 and r1c2 must contain digits lower than 6.
GAS 408 – First Impression by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2a3w5ude  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=28hebunn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A number in a grey cell must be larger than both the first cell in its row and the first cell in its column.
GAS 409 – A Lasting Impression by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/s6p943s3 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2bkrvrbv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in grey cells must have a value between the left- and right-most digits of their row, and between the top- and bottom-most digits of their column.
GAS 410 – Odd/Even Count by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p36nvxd  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ctfemmc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. An odd digit in a gray cell tells you how many of the surrounding cells (including diagonals) contain odd digits. An even digit in a gray cell tells you how many of the surrounding cells (including diagonals) contain even digits. The digit in the cell itself is not included in the count of odd or even digits.
