Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. These digits may repeat if allowed by other rules. The coloured dominoes are clones and must contain the identical digit in the identical position. (eg r4c1=r1c7=r7c4). A black dot separates cells containing digits in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one digit must be double the other). A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given. The purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. On the grey line, the sum of the digits in box 1 is equal to the sum of the digits in box 2.

[For the avoidance of doubt, the rules above DO allow different coloured clones to contain the same digits so you should not assume that eg the red clone’s digits are different to the blue clone’s digits in your solve.]

title: Another Mass of GAS
description:
Here are the URL's (both versions) for today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:

GAS 401 – Seminonconsecutive by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/4kpe7hf8 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2b58mf9o Normal sudoku rules apply. Some rows and columns are marked with '0'. Within these rows and columns, digits may never be consecutive. 
GAS 402 – Clone/Arrow by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p96tjrz  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=27yvnblw Normal sudoku rules apply. The numbers placed on the body of an arrow must add up to the number in the corresponding circle. Furthermore, the five grey shapes in the grid are all exact clones of each other - they contain the same numbers in the same relative positions. 
GAS 403 – Pastel Day by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/8c6pxkd3  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=yv8vkwp9 Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in non-white cells must be greater than digits in orthogonally adjacent white cells. (Note: If you have trouble making out which cells are highlighted - every given digit is in a non-white cell, and all other cells are white.)
GAS 404 – Makodoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/32pyjkcb  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=24na9cme Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a "+" must have a sum of less than 10. Digits separated by a "x" must have a product of less than 10. Not all + or x are necessarily given. Also, if two digits both add and multiply to values less than 10, they might be marked with a +, a x, or neither. 
GAS 405 – Quadruple Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/3uhhypx9  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=284qax3bNormal sudoku rules apply. Each number written in a white circle must appear somewhere in the four cells around that circle.

title: Another GAS Milestone
description:
Here are the URLs of the five Genuinely Approachable Puzzles today: 
GAS 396 – Extra Regions by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/5cmb6bkt https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2qdvgr85   
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey area must contain the digits from 1-9 once each.
GAS 397 – Your Grid A Splode by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3trwxzwj  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2zxrql3v 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are some lines in the grid, and each line passes through more than one of the 3x3 regions. Along each line, the digits in every region it passes through have the same sum. 
GAS 398 – Pointing Digits by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/yckbh4mr  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2lfjav2s  
Normal sudoku rules apply. If a digit N appears in a cell with an arrow, the same digit must also appear N steps away in the direction that the arrow is pointing. For instance, if a 1 appears in an arrow cell, the next cell (diagonally) in that direction must also be a 1. If a 2 appears in an arrow cell, the cell 2 steps away in that direction must also be a 2.

description:

*** Today's Sudoku ***

This puzzle (Look, Don't Kill) from Derektionary deserves some serious plaudits.  Not only does it contain an original ruleset that is the invention of the author but it keeps giving wondrous deduction after deduction.  This is a truly outstanding sudoku (and it manages to thoroughly confuse Simon!)

Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/782JMppRnf

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along arrows must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The cages in the grid are either killer cages or look-and-say cages (or both). It is up to the solver to determine which cage is which. In a killer cage, digits cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. In a Look-and-Say cage, digits CAN repeat and the small clue in the top left corner should be read as a look-and-say number (ie it says which digits are in that cage). For example, if a look-and-say cage has the clue "12" then it means there is one 2 in the cage. If it has the clue "33" then it means there are three 3s in the cage.

*** Today's Sudoku ***

KNT is producing some incredible puzzles at the moment and this extraordinary Kurotto Killer Sudoku is right up there with the best sudokus we've ever seen. Mind you, it is challenging... VERY VERY challenging.  It yields beautiful revelation after beautiful revelation though so it's well worth the time if you fancy a battle!! 

Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RpBBf44hrH

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells in the grid must be shaded. A digit in a circle indicates the total count of shaded cells in orthogonally connected groups sharing an edge with that cell. Cells with circles cannot themselves be shaded. Every orthogonally connected group of shaded or unshaded cells forms a "killer cage" ie a collection of cells in which no digit may repeat. A cell with a number in its top left corner indicates the sum of the digits in its orthogonally connected group.

title: Gaseous Glee
description:
Here are today's 5 Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) Puzzles:
GAS 391 – 00005 by Philip: http://tinyurl.com/musyx5e4 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=23r6buhw
Normal sudoku rules do not apply. Fill the grid so that each row, column, and 3x3 region contains the digits 1 through 5, as well as four blank cells. Blank cells may never share an edge. Digits in a cage may not repeat (although a cage can contain multiple blanks), and must sum to the indicated value.
GAS 392 – Liar Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3ftnaw64 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ccussmq
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage is marked with a value exactly 1 off from the correct value that goes in that cage. For instance, if a cage is marked with a 2, it must contain either a 1 or a 3. If a cage is marked with a 9, it must contain an 8.
GAS 393 – Meandering Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/39y9bpcw https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2o35raxp
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each blue region, it must be possible to draw a path that goes from 1-9 in order, travelling only horizontally and vertically.
GAS 394 – Laa Tinvaal by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/29httahf https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2f69538g
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line.
GAS 395 – Ascending Starters by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/yc5yn9wz https://f-puzzles.com/?id=23x6hppz
Normal sudoku rules apply. lues adjacent to a row or column give the sum of the run of increasing digits in that row or column, that starts in the cell closest to the clue. A run may consist of only one cell. For instance, a clue of "8" to the left of a row would be valid if the digits in that row started "8 7" or "1 2 5 4", but not if they started "8 9" (which sums to 17) or "1 3 6 2" (which sums to 10).

description:

*** Today's Sudoku ***

It's rare nowadays that we are completely surprised by a puzzle but AnalyticalNinja's Lego House is quite quite extraordinary.  Prepare to do battle with 10 puzzles to finish this sudoku and prepare to love every minute of it!

Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pbtHB6Db4g

Rules: 
Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. (Digits can repeat along arrows if allowed by other rules). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. This puzzle is solved in two stages: 1. Normal 9x9 sudoku rules DO NOT apply. Solve each 3x3 box within the grid independently (so ignoring the rest of the grid). ie Three digits (selected from 1 to 9) need to be placed in each row/column of that 3x3 box once each. 2. Erase all digits within the grid whose box number does not match their row number (eg you'll keep the digits in r4c1c2c3 within box 4). Then solve the puzzle as a regular killer arrow sudoku using the remaining digits as givens (ie normal sudoku rules will apply at this point).

title: Its the Same ... But Different
description:
Here's where you can play Same But Different by Marvin Kannhauser: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hD4NfR2JM9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are either Sandwich, X-Sums or Little Killer, one type each being red, blue and green - grey clues may be any of the types. Sandwich: the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column is 15; X-Sums: the first X digits from that direction sum to 15, where X is the first digit; Little Killer: 15 is the sum of a diagonal pointing away from the clue, which may include repeats.

description:
Here are today's 5 Genuinely Approachable (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 386 – Even Thermo by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3edwfmu9 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=29brzr7r
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase (not necessarily consecutively!), starting from the round bulb. Digits in gray squares must be even. 
GAS 387 – Killer 007 by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/3r53kmt2 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2akv2h95
Place a number from 1-7 into some cells of the grid so that every row, column and box contains each number exactly once, leaving two empty cells. Empty cells must not share an edge with each other. Numbers in a cage must add up to the given total.
GAS 388 – The Quick and the Egg by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2f8faf3n https://f-puzzles.com/?id=27adqgz4
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 389 – 0006 Killer by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/39c2574h https://f-puzzles.com/?id=25ttstt9
Fill the grid so that each row, column, and 3x3 region contains the digits 1 through 6, as well as three blank cells. Blank cells may never share an edge. Digits in a cage may not repeat (although a cage can contain multiple blanks), and must sum to the indicated value. 
GAS 390 – Zones Sudoku by Sam: http://tinyurl.com/5n89wcns https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2byrv3ab
Normal sudoku rules apply. Fill the grid so that each row, column, and 3x3 region contains the digits 1 through 6, as well as three blank cells. Blank cells may never share an edge. Digits in a cage may not repeat (although a cage can contain multiple blanks), and must sum to the indicated value.

description:
Here are today's Genuinely Approachable puzzles:
GAS 381 – Consec Pairs by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/yc3fb36b https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ooco5qb
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two cells are separated by a white dot then they must contain consecutive numbers. Cells without a dot may or may not contain consecutive numbers.
GAS 382 – Odd Thru the ❤ by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/4vmjmft4 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2bva5qsf
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given. Digits in grey circles must be odd.
GAS 383 – Anticonsecutive by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2ve5zbtm https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2amp9o4x
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a red dot are NOT consecutive. (For example, if a dot appears next to a 6, then the digit on the other side of the dot may not be a 5 or 7.) Digits without a dot may or may not be consecutive.
GAS 384 – XV Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/5n6zk2dn https://f-puzzles.com/?id=28c2bh75
Normal sudoku rules apply. When two cells are separated by the marking "XV", then the numbers in those cells must add up to 15. Cells without such a marking may or may not add up to 15.
GAS 385 – Excessivenesses by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3p7uuwcj https://f-puzzles.com/?id=28m38r5l
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a V must sum to 5, by an X must sum to 10, and by an XV must sum to 15. (No negative constraint, other pairs of digits may sum to 5, 10, or 15.)

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today we feature a hybrid puzzle from Jesper Josefsson called Aqre Fillomino.  It you remember the game Connect 4 from your childhood then the idea of this puzzle is to NOT do that!! Jesper is one of the world’s best puzzle makers and this absolutely showcases why! Give it a try at the link below: 

CtC Software: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Br6j7NpNJm

Penpa Software: https://tinyurl.com/y9bch9ee

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions, and enter a number into each empty cell, so that: Each cell contains a number equal to the number of cells in its region; no two regions of the same size share an edge; there are never more than 3 consecutive cells with the same parity within a row or a column; and all cells containing odd numbers are orthogonally connected.

title: A New Burst of GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for today's five Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 376 – Entrop Through the ❤ by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p9n4d3s https://f-puzzles.com/?id=24uesngb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given. Also, along the orange line each set of three cells must contain one high digit (789), one medium digit (456), and one low digit (123). (For example, the line could have 294396... but not 294836... because 948 does not contain a low digit). 
GAS 377 – XIIVII by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2zkmy6rc https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2do5b46v 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by an XII sum to 12. Digits separated by a VII sum to 7. Not all XIIs or VIIs are necessarily given.
GAS 378 – Thermo Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/4amfu4td https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2828oz3v 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers placed on a thermometer must strictly increase, starting from the bulb end.
GAS 379 – Lixiviatin’ on a Prayer by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p923dy6 https://f-puzzles.com/?id=22xpqrkq 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given. Also, there are some lines in the grid, and each line passes through more than one of the 3x3 regions. Along each line, the digits in every region it passes through have the same sum. (For instance, r2c7+r2c8+r3c9 = r4c9+r5c9+r6c8).
GAS 380 – XIIIVIII by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5n7uszsp https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2ytyg8qd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on either side of an XIII sum to 13. Digits on either side of a VIII sum to 8. Not all XIIIs or VIIIs are necessarily given.

title: The Battle to End All Battles
description:
Here's where you can play Duel of the Fates by Darth Paradox: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mhd2mbpddH 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each arrow must sum to the number in its circle. There are six different colors of lines in this puzzle. Each color corresponds to a different one of these constraints: - Dutch Whispers (adjacent numbers on the line must differ by at least 4); - Entropic (any three adjacent digits on the line must be one each of 1-3, 4-6, and 7-9); - German Whispers (adjacent numbers on the line must differ by at least 5); - Palindrome (the numbers on the line form the same sequence no matter which end you start from); - Region Sums (if the line passes through multiple regions, the sum of the digits on the line must be the same in each region); - Renban (the line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order with no repeats).

Here are URL's for todays 5 Genuinely Approachable Sudokus (GAS) in our software and in f-puzzles:
GAS 371 – Mathrax by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2s4hsfze https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2d7vgaxh 
Each time a + sign appears in the grid, look at the four cells surrounding it. Of those four cells, the two pairs diagonally opposite each other have the same sum. For instance, a + could have 1 and a 7 diagonally opposite each other, and a 3 and a 5 diagonally opposite each other, since both of these pairs sum to 8.
GAS 372 – Classic Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/3j57es4f  https://f-puzzles.com/?id=2d8trol4

GAS 374 – XIVI by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5beuv8xa https://f-puzzles.com/?id=27rtxwr4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on either side of an XI sum to 11. Digits on either side of a VI sum to 6. Not all XIs or VIs are necessarily given.

title: Revolutionary Sudoku Techniques?
description:
Here's where you can try Bastille Day by Full Deck and Missing a Few Cards: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/PNnGjgLp2Q 
Bastille Day (14 July) commemorates the storming of the Bastille fortress in Paris in 1789. There was some debate and it was almost celebrated on 5 May instead. Boxes 1 and 9 are firework explosions, while boxes 3 and 7 contain the fleur-de-lis often associated with the fallen French monarchy. Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue (fortress) cells must be larger than orthogonally adjacent non-blue cells. Digits on thermometers must increase from bulb to tip, not necessarily consecutively.

title: A GAS celebration
description:
Here are the URLs for today's puzzles:
GAS 366 – G, as in GAS by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5n767956 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase (not necessarily consecutively), starting from the round bulb. Digits separated by a black dot must be in a 1:2 ratio. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given. 
A, as in 'A GAS' by Philip
https://tinyurl.com/zwpk5zyw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the value in the attached circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow if they follow sudoku rules. A digit in a white circle must appear within the four cells surrounding that circle. 
S, as in 'Still GAS' by Sam
https://tinyurl.com/2p969u3b 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all X’s and V’s are necessarily given. Neighboring digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. 
GAS 367 – Susurration by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/42s93vmr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells directly connected by a green line must differ by at least 5.
GAS 368 – Max Ascending by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p986suj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, a clue outside of a row or column gives the length of the longest contiguous 'run' of increasing digits in that row or column, from the direction of the clue. For instance, if a '6' appears to the left of a row, then there must be a run of 6 increasing digits somewhere in that row, such as 2 4 5 6 8 9. However, there must NOT be a run of 7 increasing digits in that row, since the 6 indicates the longest run.
GAS 369 – Odd-Even Star Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/4znbsra9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If a star contains an odd number then the (up to) four numbers around it must be even, and if a star contains an even number then the (up to) four numbers around it must be odd.

title: Learn To Solve Pencil Puzzles: The Best Of The Best
description:
Today Simon turns again to the Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzles published on the channel "Daily Pencil Puzzle Discussion" on the Cracking The Cryptic Fan Discord server.  This channel publishes one new puzzle every day and they are an absolute treat.  These puzzles have been recommended to us as the best of the last few months!

You can join the Discord server here:
https://discord.gg/BbN89j5

If you enjoy this video there are more pencil puzzle videos on the channel (just search for Pencil Puzzles!) and on Patreon.

Puzzle 1: Uso-One by shye

Example: https://tinyurl.com/5n77fy8t
Main Puzzle: https://tinyurl.com/33jk5zmt

Rules: Shade some cells so that no two shaded cells are orthogonally adjacent and the remaining unshaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Clued cells cannot be shaded, and represent the number of shaded cells in the (up to) four cells orthogonal to the clue. However, exactly one clue in each region is incorrect.

Puzzle 2: Juosan by jovi_al

Example: https://tinyurl.com/asatajuz
Main Puzzle: https://tinyurl.com/2p8xd7u8

Rules: Place a horizontal or vertical line into each cell, traveling from edge to edge. A number in a region represents how many horizontal or vertical lines it contains - whichever there’s at least half of. There may not exist a run of three consecutive cells containing parallel distinct lines anywhere in the grid.

Puzzle 3: Battleships by Tyrgannus

Example: https://tinyurl.com/2p8uy8wz
Main Puzzle: https://tinyurl.com/rr2j8xyr

Rules: Place the given fleet of ships into the grid so that no two ships are touching, not even diagonally. Rotating ships is permitted. A clue outside the grid indicates the number of cells in the corresponding row or column that are occupied by ships. Cells with waves cannot be occupied by a ship. A given ship segment must be used as the part of a ship that its shape represents.

Puzzle 4: Summon by Freddie Hand

Example: https://tinyurl.com/3rx759xx
Main Puzzle: https://tinyurl.com/yckzhkfa

Rules: Enter the given set of digits into the grid, so that each digit appears exactly once in each region. Cells with equal digits cannot touch each other, not even diagonally. Digits in adjacent cells within a row or column form multi-digit numbers, read from left to right or from top to bottom; digits without neighbours form single-digit numbers. The numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of all such multi-digit and single-digit numbers in the respective row or column.

Puzzle 5: Square Jam by Eric Fox 

Example: https://tinyurl.com/2s446y9d
Main Puzzle: https://tinyurl.com/msx7j4bd

Rules: Divide the grid into square regions of orthogonally connected cells. A number indicates the side length of the square it’s in. Region borders may not form any four-way intersections.

title: Can You Name A Better Puzzle?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This is the one you've all asked for!  Yin Yang by Jesper is surely one of the most brilliant and extraordinary sudoku puzzles ever.  A quite ludicrous ruleset which constantly begs the question - HOW did he create this? Just one point:  It's not very easy :)

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/t4GP9DgL9j

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Shade some cells so the following conditions are all fulfilled: All shaded cells are connected; all unshaded cells are connected; no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded; and each region is either fully shaded or fully unshaded. The digit in a cell with one or more arrows is equal to the total number of shaded cells that appear in the indicated directions combined (not including the arrow cell itself). Not all possible arrows/arrow combinations are given.

There is an example on this page:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009Z9

*** PATREON REWARDS JUST OUT ***

title: Brand New Sudoku Rules = Brand New Logic
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An incredible new rule today from Agent... the puzzle is called Imprisoned and it's just got the most beautiful solve path. Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QrH7dgjtLb

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum total of the digits in the cage that contains the Nth cell from that direction, where N is the first digit from that direction. eg if r9c5 = 3 then the sum of the digits in the cage containing r7c5 (the 3rd cell vertically from r9c5) would be 26.

There is an example on this page:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000ADA

title: A Great Year of GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for puzzles 361 to 365, which complete the first year of Genuinely Approachable Sudoku:
GAS 361 – Entropic Lines by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/mtfycpcw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line contains exactly one low digit (123), one medium digit (456), and one high digit (789), in any order. 
GAS 362 – Kropki Pairs by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/4y3mj3a5 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive numbers. Cells separated by a black dot must contain numbers in a 1:2 ratio. Cells without markings may or may not contain numbers with such a relationship.
GAS 363 – Epic Crossover by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/6x5kvvep 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive (have a difference of 1); digits in cells separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. (No negative constraint - other pairs of digits may also be consecutive or have a 2:1 ratio.) 
GAS 364 – Star Battle by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/4fhtpvxh 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, 8 and 9 must never touch themselves or each other, even diagonally.
GAS 365 – Skyscrapers Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/ycxnmakh 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each number in the grid represents a building of that height, and clues outside the grid indicate how many buildings are visible when looking from that point along the corresponding row or column. A building is visible when there are no taller buildings before it.

title: The Sudoku Made Of ONLY 5 Green Lines
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today we try a puzzle consisting of just 5 green lines!  It's called Submarine Sandwiches and it's by Nordy.  How does it work? Well you'll have to try it to see - it IS approachable :) Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/m3BfHFrP8D

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. (Within the 9x9 grid, place the digits 1 to 9 in every row, column and 3x3 box). Each of the ten cells outside the 9x9 grid must contain a digit from 1 to 9 inclusive. The outer digits can be repeated as necessary. Each outer digit gives the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in its corresponding row/column. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5.

description:
Here's where you can try Chaos Power by Panthera: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QLMfpLdG9R 
1-9 appear in each row and column. Japanese Sums rules: The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs found in that row or column that must be shaded. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs. If a row or column is unclued, there is no shading in that row or column. Regions, which each contain 1-9 orthogonally connected, must be determined. Either all or no cells within a region are shaded. There is a 3x3 magic square (all 3-cell rows, columns and diagonals sum to the same number) hidden somewhere in the picture.

title: 360 Degrees of GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for GAS puzzles 356-360 (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku):
GAS 356 – Parquet Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2grxnkau 
Fill each cell with a number from 1 to 9 so that each of the 12 rows and columns, as well as the 9 regions, contains every number exactly once. Some cells span more than one row or column, and the number in that cell is counted as part of every row and column that the cell stretches over.
GAS 357 – Tilting at Windoku by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/38nnmtpw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each colored region must contain the digits 1-9 exactly once each. (Note: The central orange region is connected diagonally!)
GAS 358 – Frameless by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/y3tf4xw8 
1-9 appears in each row, column and marked region. If a clue appears outside of a row or column, then the first X cells in that direction must sum to the value of that clue. X may or may not be different for different clues, and its value(s) must be determined by the solver. For example, if a '9' appears above a column, then the topmost cell in that column could be a 9; or the top two cells in the column could be 3 and 6; or the top three cells could be 1, 2, and 6; etc. 
GAS 359 – Pyramid Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/3a3r84w8 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If a grey cell has two grey cells immediately diagonally beneath it, then the number in the top cell must be the difference of the numbers in the bottom two cells.
GAS 360 – Substitution by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/bddj565n 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the nearest X numbers in the corresponding row or column, where X is the nearest of those numbers.
Round 4 of the Sudoku Mahabharat is at https://logicmastersindia.com/live/?contest=SM202204.

title: Finding the Problem can be Harder than Solving It
description:

title: The Miracle Latin Square
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Perhaps one of the strangest and most brilliant puzzles we've ever attempted on the channel today.  It's called 3 Snakes 2 Puzzles by the_cogito and, when you read the rules, it's hard to believe it has a unique solution.  Simon attempts it with Covid-brain - which is ambitious :)

Play the puzzle at the link below: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/N9BtFhRG4L

Rules: 
Place each digit 1-9 exactly once in every row and column. Divide the grid into 3 snakes, which don't overlap and which collectively cover the entire grid. A snake is a 1-cell wide path of orthogonally connected cells with no branching. A snake may not touch itself, even diagonally. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 2:1 ratio. Cells containing grey circles must contain odd digits. Thick borders between cells indicate those cells are a part of two different snakes. Adjacent cells along the same snake must contain digits that differ by exactly 4 or 5. 


If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

It's a classic sudoku with a very cool trick.  On Patreon we've released a solve video showing Mark's solve (not knowing the trick) and then Simon's explanation of how to go about it differently :)

title: Great Balls of GAS
description:
Here are the URLs where you can play today's five GAS (genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 351 – The Anduin by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3zdwhjve 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, there are some lines in the grid, and each line passes through more than one of the 3x3 regions. Along each line, the digits in every region it passes through have the same sum. For instance, r5c1 + r4c2 = r3c2 + r3c3 + r2c3. 
GAS 352 – Between by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2rysp6an 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values in between the values in the attached circles. For instance, if the circles on the ends of a line contain 1 and 7, then the digits along that line can only include 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.
GAS 353 – Your Brain on Sudoku by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/ykbdhh6e 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given.
GAS 354 – Arrow Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p8wpwuy
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers on the body of an arrow must add up to the number in the attached circle.
GAS 355 – Tic Tac Toe by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/25hmmc98 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits on each gray line have the same parity (either all odd or all even). If the digits on a gray line in a region are all odd (or even), then the digit in the corresponding cell in the central region is odd (or even). (For example, if the digits on the gray line in the top right box are all odd, then the digit in the top right cell of the central box must also be odd.)

title: To Infinity And Beyond!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Occasionally we love to try non-sudoku puzzles on the channel and that's what we get to do today with this quite wonderful fillomino/star battle hybrid by au voleur.  This has a perfect rating on Logic Masters Germany and for good reason, it's an absolute blast!

Play the puzzle at the link below: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HJfhP4DRpF

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions called polyominoes so that no two polyominoes with the same area share an edge. Inside some cells are given numbers; each number must represent the area of the polyomino it belongs to. A polyomino may contain zero, one, or more of the given numbers. Also, every row, column and polyomino must contain exactly 2 shaded cells. Shaded cells cannot touch, even diagonally. 

If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

title: Monopoly Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely astonishing sudoku today in which constructor Trevor Nicholas has merged sudoku with Monopoly.  And what's so clever about this is that the rules are thematic and related to the game itself (and the puzzle is fairly difficult!)

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

With extra graphics (thanks to Sven for creating this link):
https://sudokupad.app/MONOPOLYSUDOKU

Without the extra graphics:
https://sudokupad.app/MONOPOLYSUDOKU2

Plain old grid:
https://tinyurl.com/5h686jhm

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Additionally:

• Arrow: Pass Go, Collect $200! Digits on the arrow multiply to 200.

• Properties: All property sets, including the Utilities set (gray), contain consecutive digits in any order (eg 2,3,1). Each set contains a different group of digits.

• Chance (?): Digits in Chance cells reveal the row, column, and digit (in some combination) of a hidden cell. eg If the Chance digits were 1,2 & 3 the hidden cell would be one of: r1c2=3; r1c3=2; r2c1=3; r2c3=1; r3c1=2; & r3c2=1.

• Railroads (RR): Each RR cell connects to one other RR cell through a 1-cell wide “track.” Digits on a track must form a palindrome (digits read the same forwards and backwards) starting & ending with RR cells. Tracks cannot touch themselves/each other orthogonally and cannot pass through properties, cages, or Chance cells.


If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

title: The Lie Detector
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A return of Niverio to the channel tonight with Liar Spiral, in which every clue type has exactly one liar in the grid.  This makes from some seriously clever logic although be careful - it's easy to make a mistake!!

Play the puzzle at the link below: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8hNMDjTnbM

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following clue types has exactly one liar in the puzzle: Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle; adjacent digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2; cells with a grey square contain even digits; adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5; clues outside the grid indicate the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction; cells with a grey circle contain odd digits; digits in a white circle must appear in at least one of the four surrounding cells (for this clue type to be correct, all digits in the circle must satisfy this condition); cells along a purple line must be a set of consecutive digits; digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end; cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5; cells connected by a white dot have to contain consecutive digits; and cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10.

If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

It's a classic sudoku with a very cool trick.  On Patreon we've released a solve video showing Mark's solve (not knowing the trick) and then Simon's explanation of how to go about it differently :)

title: GAS takes Sudoku to a New Dimension
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 GAS puzzles (two are in Penpa):
GAS 346 – Isodoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/yxwhqkn8 
Fill the grid with the digits 1 through 8, so that each 2x4 region contains each digit once. Also, each "row" and "column" contains each digit once. Example rows and columns are shown in the example image (there are four lines in each of three directions, each of which contains the digits once each.) 
GAS 347 – Fortress Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/59m7v3bz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Whenever a shaded cell is horizontally or vertically next to an unshaded cell, then the shaded cell must contain the higher number.
GAS 348 – Leg Day by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/ps88z7u3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in corner circles must appear in the surrounding four cells, in some order.
GAS 349 – Sudokurve by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/yyokubfp 
Fill the grid with the digits 1 through 9, so that each digit appears exactly once in each 3x3 region, "row," and "column." Rows and columns continue from one section to another as indicated by the green lines (in the example image, a row and a column have been indicated with shading). 
GAS 350 – Consec Pairs by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2da8vbvc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in cells connected by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all such pairs are necessarily marked.

title: The 100%-Rated Human-Solvable Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It was always going to be difficult to follow yesterday's ridiculous puzzle by Jay Dyer but, when you need a genius to help you out, the TotallyNormalCat is a reliable creature!  Their latest puzzle (called Boiga Irregularis) is 100% rated on Logic Masters Germany but is only of average difficulty - a rare combination indeed.  

Play the puzzle at the link below: 
https://tinyurl.com/3ufffx2y

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell wide snake of orthogonally connected cells which doesn't touch itself orthogonally; the path begins in r9c1 and ends in r9c7. Adjacent snake cells must differ by at least 5. A digit in a circle is equal to the number of snake cells in the (up to) 9 surrounding cells, including itself. The snake must visit each circle. 

If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

It's a classic sudoku with a very cool trick.  On Patreon we've released a solve video showing Mark's solve (not knowing the trick) and then Simon's explanation of how to go about it differently :)

title: A Sudoku Whose ONLY Clue Is A Single Line???
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This might be the most ridiculous sudoku we've ever featured.  Simon is still shaking his head about this puzzle actually existing.  The Miracle Sudoku was miraculous but this... this is SO ludicrous... welcome to Jörmungandr by Jay Dyer.  Prepare to have your mind blown.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 
https://tinyurl.com/yt5dzj2f

Rules: 
Contained within the grid are nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, which must be located. Each region contains the digits 1-9 once each such that no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions do not contain digits. Along the line, each time the line passes through a region, the sum of the digits on that pass sum to the same value. If the line passes through a region multiple times, each pass is summed separately.


If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

title: Pythagoras' Nightmare
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for Matthias J. Raives and a simply wonderful puzzle involving pythagorean triples!  At first it'll seem completely intractable but there is a way :) 

Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bntpQqtDT4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of digits along each edge of a triangle must form a Pythagorean triple, with the largest number of the triple corresponding to the sum along the hypotenuse. There are 12 triangles in this puzzle. Some pythagorean triples include the following (and the multiples thereof): (3,4,5); (5,12,13); (8,15,17); and (7,24,25). 

If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

It's a classic sudoku with a very cool trick.  On Patreon we've released a solve video showing Mark's solve (not knowing the trick) and then Simon's explanation of how to go about it differently :)

title: Blackadder: The Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We are on the most incredible run of absolutely extraordinary sudokus and we've found another one today with udukos' latest, titled "Blackadder"! You will need a cunning plan that is very much NOT a la Baldrick to have a hope of solving this one :)

Give it a try at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/2p85dfpe

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The cells with a clue in the top left corner represent one end of a snake. Each clue belongs to a different snake. The value of the clue gives the sum of all the digits that lie on a snake. These snakes behave as region sum lines. As a snake passes through different 3 x 3 boxes, digits on the snake have an equal sum N within each box it passes through. If the snake passes through the same box more than once, then each individual segment within that box sums to N separately. The snake must pass through at least two 3 x 3 boxes. If '?' is given as a clue, then its value has to be deduced. The snakes can't touch themselves orthogonally or diagonally. Two snakes can't share a cell together.

The example puzzle can be found at the following link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009YL

If you manage to solve this one and want more sudoku then give this puzzle from Sam Cavnar-Johnson a try:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HM2hg3Pngf

It's a classic sudoku with a very cool trick.  On Patreon we've released a solve video showing Mark's solve (not knowing the trick) and then Simon's explanation of how to go about it differently :)

title: "One Of My All-Time Favourite Puzzles"
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The incredible run of astonishing sudokus continues with another puzzle from the new constructor lerroyy, who is wowing the sudoku world at the moment. You can see from the start of the video what some of the great sudoku solvers/setters are saying about this sudoku (which is called "Windmill"). 

Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LjR6P6LqN7

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits cannot repeat on the main diagonal (marked in blue). Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.

title: The Incredible Windmill Sudoku Discovery
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
SSG has made a discovery that we'd like to share with you all today.  This puzzle is called Tilting and it is absolutely incredible that it exists. The rotational symmetry is there for all to see and yet it solves uniquely (and beautifully).  This is another astonishing puzzle, do give it a try at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/2cdw5pcp

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in circles must appear at least once in the surrounding four cells. Digits in cages may not repeat. In each cage, digits are grouped into pairs of adjacent cells - each cell used exactly once. Each pair is a two-digit number, read left-to-right or top-to-bottom. The sum of the two-digit numbers is given in the upper left corner of the cage.

title: The Great GASby
description:
Here are the URLs for all today's (8!) GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 336 – BIG3 Sudoku by Philip: 
https://tinyurl.com/2h9jb83u 
https://tinyurl.com/44rrs6e5 
https://tinyurl.com/mrxs66n4 
https://tinyurl.com/yc666myn 
1-6 appears in each row, column and marked region. X-Sums: Clues outside the grid tell you the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding row or column, starting with the digit adjacent to the clue and continuing away from the clue, where X is the adjacent digit. (For example: ?????7534 (19) would be a valid fill for a row where 19 is the sum of the rightmost 4 digits.) Sandwich: Clues outside the grid tell you the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 6 in that row or column, not including the 1 and 6 themselves. Skyscrapers: Each number you place into the grid represents the height of a building. Clues outside the grid tell you how many buildings can be "seen" in the corresponding row or column when looking from that direction; taller buildings block the view of any smaller buildings behind them. Little Killer: Clues outside the grid tell you the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal (digits may repeat if allowed by other rules).
GAS 337 – Equal Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2czz5ubz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Within each cage, the sum of the odd digits is equal to the sum of the even digits. 
GAS 338 – Clone Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p849yt2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The two grey areas must contain exactly the same numbers in the same places.
GAS 339 – Return of the King by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/bdhfwn79 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in diagonally adjacent cells cannot be the same. (In other words, a digit cannot touch itself, even diagonally.)
GAS 340 – Product/Sum by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/mtx9ucu8 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages marked with a "+" give the sum (addition) of all of the digits within that cage. Cages marked with a "x" give the product (multiplication) of all of the digits within that cage.

title: Math Professor Sets Impossible Sudoku
description:
*** PATREON REWARDS JUST OUT ***
Join us on Patreon to participate in the two new competitions!  We have two amazing sudoku packs from Panthera, TheAsylum and grkles themed around Japanese Sum Sudoku (which make pictures in the grid if you solve them correctly!). 

We've also got Mark's Platinum Jubilee Sudoku and a video on how it was made. 

Just $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There are a very small number of setters in the world of sudoku whose puzzles are always (and we mean ALWAYS) excellent.  Zetamath is such a setter - his sudokus are a joy but, as a rule, quite hard... Simon, on his birthday (21 again), risks attempting zeta's latest, MIA!  

Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://zetamath.link/mia

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw some killer cages into the grid. Each killer cage is a set of one or more orthogonally connected cells. Killer cages do not overlap and do not contain repeated digits. Every killer cage touches at least one dot. Every dot lies on a boundary between two cages. A white dot between two cages indicates that their totals are consecutive. A black dot between two cages indicates that their totals have a ratio of 2:1. All possible dots are given. Eg if an edge has a different cage on both sides, and those cages have consecutive totals, there will always be a white dot there. Every killer cage contains its size as a digit. Eg a cage of size 3 cells must contain a 3. The shaded cell in r9c5 is not part of any cage. 

There is an example puzzle at this link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000A0E

title: The Caduceus Entanglement
description:
*** PATREON REWARDS JUST OUT ***
Mark's Jubilee Sudoku out tonight + video of how he created the puzzle coming on Tues/Wed!

Also you can participate in the two new competitions!  We have two amazing sudoku packs from Panthera, TheAsylum and grkles themed around Japanese Sum Sudoku (which make pictures in the grid if you solve them correctly!). Just $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Caduceus by PjotrV is a 100% rated puzzle on Logic Masters Germany and for good reason.  This is simply superb sudoku AND it involves not one but two snakes :)  Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jRhnH89mNm

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Furthermore, there are two snakes (snake A and B) in the grid. One is an 'Equal Sum Line' Snake (see below) and the other is a 'German Whisper Line' Snake (again, see below). The solver must determine which is which. Each snake is an orthogonally connected set of cells (the starts and ends are marked) and each snake MUST visit every 3x3 box. The snakes cannot touch themselves, even diagonally. The snakes may touch each other but they do not cross each other. The outside clues give the sum of the NON-snake cells in that direction. The squares give the number of the NON-snake cells in that box. On an 'Equal Sum Line', digits have an equal sum N within each box the line passes through. On a German Whisper Line, adjacent digits must have a difference of at least 5.

title: GASworks (only sometimes it doesn't)
description:
Here are today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 331 – Consec Thermo by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2k3pyhye 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along each thermo must increase CONSECUTIVELY from the round bulb to the tip: for instance, a thermo could contain the sequence 3 4 5 6, but not 3 4 5 7. 
GAS 332 – Quadro Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/4jh98hsz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. No 2x2 area of the grid is allowed to contain all odd numbers or all even numbers.
GAS 333 – The Arrow of Hat Time by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/ye2yy7zk 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along arrows must sum to the circled total.
GAS 334 – Full or Half by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5n6cz3d7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If a square appears at the intersection of four cells, then exactly two of those cells have even digits, and exactly two of them have odd digits (not necessarily in a 'checkerboard' pattern.) If a circle appears at the intersection of four cells, then all four of those cells have the same parity: either all odd, or all even.
GAS 335 – Sequence Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/3u8yt87h 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line must consist of an arithmetic sequence; that is, a sequence of numbers with a constant difference between each of the terms, like 1-2-3-4 or 3-5-7-9. The sequence can begin at either end of a line.

description:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/P4FrjqFPRh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The red line is an oscillator line, along which digits alternate being high (more than 5) and low (less than 5). Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal (and may include repeated digits if permitted by other rules). Digits may not repeat along the main diagonal marked in blue. Grey lines are palindromes, which read the same forwards and backwards. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. title: Endgame: The Sudoku With The MOST Crazy Finale
description:
*** PATREON REWARDS JUST OUT ***
Join us on Patreon to participate in the two new competitions!  We have two amazing sudoku packs from Panthera, TheAsylum and grkles themed around Japanese Sum Sudoku (which make pictures in the grid if you solve them correctly!). Just $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
KNT has been making incredible sudoku since just March 2022.  Every single one of KNT's puzzles has an enormously high rating on Logic Masters Germany and this is a great example of why. Spelunker is astonishing - the logic at the start is fabulous but the logic at the end.... Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/k3j46ntb

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some of the cells must be coloured grey so that all grey cells (the “walls”) are orthogonally connected to the edge and all other (green) cells form an orthogonally connected area (the “cave”). Grey cells may not have 2x2 blocks. A number in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits that are seen from this cell looking to the north, south, east, and west. The cell with the clue counts once in this sum. Walls obstruct the view. A cell with a clue must be part of the cave. Within the field of vision of a clue, digits may not repeat. In addition, any two orthogonally adjacent wall cells must have values that differ by at least 5. Isolated wall cells are not bound to any constraint.

title: Oh No! Everything Is Wrogn AGAIN!!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Simon faces his nemesis again tonight with another Wrogn sudoku - this time from Lerroyy.  A Wrogn puzzle is one in which all the rules are the opposite to normal - which is, frankly, terrifying.  This is (yet) another example of setters demonstrating the total genius when it comes to these sudoku variants.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/g8LBNq46FM

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot cannot be consecutive. Digits separated by black dot cannot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits separated by X may not sum to 10. Digits separated by V may not sum to 5. Digits in a cage may not sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along a red line may not form a palindrome. Digits in a yellow “max” cell must be smaller than ALL the orthogonally adjacent cells. Digits in an orange “min” cell must be bigger than ALL the orthogonally adjacent cells. Digits in a circle cannot ALL appear in the surrounding cells and no digit in the 4 surrounding cells can repeat. Along each grey thermometer is a bulb (it is NOT the current one and has to be found); digits must increase from that bulb to the extremities and may not repeat. Digits along a purple line may not repeat and must not form a set of consecutive digits. Clues outside the grid must not give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. A cell with a blue square must not contain an even digit.

title: Is there GAS at Rascasse?
description:
Here's where you can play today's 5 GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 326 – Consec Pairs by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/yc7mc5m8 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all dots are given.
GAS 327 – Lampropeltis Holbrooki by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3crsw4hp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive (have a difference of 1); digits in cells separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. (No negative constraint - other pairs of digits may also be consecutive or have a 2:1 ratio.)
GAS 328 – Sequence by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p9x34n9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each line form an evenly spaced sequence (such as 1 3 5 7 or 2 5 8), increasing in the direction that the arrow is pointing.
GAS 329 – Classic Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/yc294vb7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 330 – Nonzero Sum Game by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/y5a9c8h5 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding row or column, starting with the digit adjacent to the clue and continuing away from the clue, where X is the adjacent digit. For example: ?????7534 (19) would be a valid fill for a row where 19 is the sum of the rightmost 4 digits.

description:

title: GAS Patchy
description:
Here's where you can try GAS 321 – Ocean’s Trio by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/4uhc2yr4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, consecutive digits must never be orthogonally adjacent. The digits 1, 2, and 3 are marked with orange circles; the digits 4, 5, and 6 are marked with blue squares.
GAS 322 – Sum Frame by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/k6dh9vzk  
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value outside of the grid gives the sum of the first three digits from that direction (closest to the clue) in that row or column. For instance, because a '22' clue appears to the right of row 7, the sum of the digits in row 7, columns 7/8/9 must be 22. 
GAS 323 – Rossini Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/52264n43 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If an arrow is given outside the grid, then the three cells nearest the arrow in that row or column increase in the direction of the arrow. All possible arrows are given! This means that where no arrow is shown, the three digits neither increase nor decrease. For example, there is no arrow to the left of row 4, so the first three digits in row 4 are in neither increasing nor decreasing order.
GAS 324 – Guard Dog by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/mtfvuc8c 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a black dot must have the ratio given; digits in cells separated by a white dot must have the difference given.
GAS 325 – Max Arrow by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p92bcah 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit in the round bulb of each arrow, tells you what the *largest* digit is along the line attached to that arrow. Eg: if there's a '6' in an arrow bulb, then there has to be at least one additional 6 somewhere along the arrow line, and all of the other digits along the line must be less than 6.

title: Could You Help Me?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

A very original and interesting sudoku today from SSG called Covert Confinement.  It mixes up Sudoku, Nurikabe, X-Sums and Killer rules and we love it! And you might be able to help Simon spot what he thinks he's missed at the end of the solve.... :)

Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MD2fPgdNbf

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells form a single orthogonally-connected region and no 2x2 square is fully shaded. Each unshaded region must contain exactly one clue cell. Each unshaded region is an “X-killer cage”. title: The Puzzle Of Perpetual Motion
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Sumanta Mukherjee has made some astonishing puzzles recently and this one takes the biscuit. It's called Perpetual Motion Of Kind '0' - which someone will have to explain - and it contains some simply extraordinary logic. Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BthBMRbt7M

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. A black dot separates cells containing digits with a 1:2 ratio. A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. Digits on a blue line must be numerically in between the two circled cells at the line's ends. The orange line contains three consecutive digits in any order. The biggest of those digits is divisible by 3. The inequality sign points to the lower of the two digits.

title: Overdue GAS Bill
description:
Here are the five URLs for today's GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 316 – Median by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5xehesp7
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. In each cage, the indicated value is the median (middle) digit in that cage. For instance, a cage containing the digits 2, 7, and 8 would be marked with a '7', and a cage containing the digits 1, 5, and 7 would be marked with a '5'.
GAS 317 – Palindrome Quads by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2b96sjwv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers on a grey line must form a palindromic sequence. Numbers in a white circle must appear in one of the four cells around the circle.
GAS 318 – Cross Hares by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p8rmrpa  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given.
GAS 319 – Nonconsec Trio by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/muksw5dj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Consecutive digits may never touch orthogonally. The digits 1, 2, and 3 are marked with orange circles; the digits 4, 5, and 6 are marked with blue squares.
GAS 320 – XV Killer Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p926emc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in a cage must add up to the indicated total. Numbers separated by a V must add up to 5. Numbers separated by an X must add up to 10.

title: The Masterpiece
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

This is a special one.  Nahileon's Archery Target looks absolutely impossible to even start.  Simon considers stopping the video after he deduces ONE thing about it after 30 minutes because that deduction is so beautiful he's scared it'll be lost forever if he fails to finish the puzzle.  You may never forget this sudoku and can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Hdpt6h9nBt

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey line in the central box is a thermometer. Digits along that thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip, but the positions of the bulb and the tip are hidden. In the outer three rings, the sum of the digits along a ring between two 9s must always be the same throughout the puzzle. For the avoidance of doubt, those two 9s could be the same 9 if a ring has only a single 9 in it.

You can see an example of a possible grid here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009QI

title: Watch A World Sudoku/Puzzle Champion Solving!
description:
*** Bonus Video ***

We're thrilled to share this video with you which includes footage of Thomas Snyder - 3x World Sudoku Champion and former World Puzzle Champion, in speed-solving mode.  The puzzle he attempts is a Tapa Sudoku by Serkan Yurekli - and it is NOT an easy solve.  More on that below...  

Serkan has just released a puzzle pack of Easy/Medium Tapa puzzles  (and he invented Tapa!), which you can get here:

https://shop.gmpuzzles.com/collections/smaller-puzzle-collections/products/starter-pack-2-tapa

We tried to work out how best to show this video - recognising that in this unusual puzzle type it would be difficult to follow the logic.  Originally our plan was to use footage of Simon's solving video but this proved beyond our editing capabilities to do properly.  So what we present here is Thomas' solve with Simon commentating over the top.  Thomas does a LOT of logic here incredibly fast so, if you prefer a slower pace, Simon's solve is available on Patreon (see below).  Overall though our strong recommendation would be for you all to try the puzzle.  This will give you the best insight into the extraordinary calculation speed Thomas is employing here.  Big thanks to Serkan and Thomas for making this video possible.

You can try Tapa Sudoku at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/L64LJ4LQ4t

Rules: 
[Please note these rules are quite complicated and a familiarity with Tapa will definitely be helpful.]

Tapa: Shade some empty cells grey to create a single connected wall. The shaded cells cannot form a 2x2 square anywhere in the grid. Numbers in a circled cell indicate the length of consecutive shaded blocks in the neighboring cells. If there is more than one number in a circled cell, then there must be at least one white (unshaded) cell between the grey cell groups.  Also, all unshaded cells of the grid should contain all digits from 1 to 7 in each row and column. All cells marked with circles should contain at least one digit (and therefore they are not shaded). The digits in circles are valid clues for Tapa and pencilmark clues for sudoku. You should place one or more digits in the empty circles but you cannot make additions to given circle clues. All possible circled cells may not be given (ie there may be some cells without circles that are valid clues for both the Tapa and sudoku.)

GM Puzzles produces puzzles under a CC licence (https://tinyurl.com/3pj3byec). No changes have been made to this puzzle.

title: The Cave Manipulation
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

A breathtaking idea today from Abed Hawila who somehow has made a puzzle combing sudoku - with a region sum line constraint - with the logic puzzle Cave.  This has a long rule set but don't be put off.  If you read the rules a couple of times (and look at the example linked below, if necessary), you'll see it's actually fairly intuitive and an absolute blast to solve. You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FB378fm267

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some of the cells must be coloured grey so that all grey cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge and all other (green) cells form an orthogonally connected area (the cave). Grey cells may not form 2x2 blocks. A number in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits that are “seen” from this cell looking to the north, south, east, and west. The cell with the clue counts once in this sum. Walls obstruct the view. A cell with a clue must be part of the cave. Within the field of vision of a clue, digits may not repeat. In addition, grey walls act as “Region Sum lines”: Meaning that each wall (ie group of connected grey squares) must visit at least two boxes and the sum of the digits in each box must be equal.

An example grid can be found here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009VE

title: Sudoku is in the Genes
description:
Here's where you can try out Genetics by Angelo: https://tinyurl.com/24r8hh8y 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit has two properties. The first property is being odd or even. The second property is being low (1,2,3), medium (4,5,6) or high (7,8,9). Each cell that is directly connected to two cells in the row above it is considered a child of those two cells (the parents). Each child can be formed by taking a property of one parent and taking the other property of the other parent.
Some clarifying examples: Parents with values 2 and 5 can have a 6 as a child, as the 6 gets the even property from the 2 and the medium property from the 5. Parents with values 1 and 5 can have a 1 as a child, as the child 1 gets the low property from the 1 and the odd property from the 5. Parents with values 3 and 8 could have two children with values 7 and 9, but they could also have two children with values 2 and 7.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

A REALLY clever sudoku today from Niverio where you'll need to be able to work out some simple factors to make progress.  You can try it at the link below:

title: The Phistomefel Meta Conundrum
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

Another chance to bathe in the genius of Phistomefel this evening as Simon takes on his sudoku, Greedy Cages. This is a long video (for which Simon apologises!) but some of the ideas in this puzzle are REALLY interesting. (In particular, drop a comment if you can see a neat way of proving what Simon finds out about one of the cages at the start!) You can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/g2NBLTF6h8

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues in the top left corner of a cell mean that that cell is part of a cage whose digits sum to that clue's value. A cage is an orthogonally connected set of cells in which no digit may repeat. Each cage contains exactly one given clue. Cages do not overlap. If a clue is a question mark it is unclear how large the sum of the respective cage is. The cages are "greedy" ie digits in a cage cannot appear in any orthogonally adjacent cells or cages.

title: The Sudoku With Just 2 Digits And A Small Hat?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

A fascinating puzzle today called Smallhat by the_cogito. What is going on with these enormous lines in the grid and where are the 3x3 boxes?! You can try it at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/ysuszmhy

Rules: 
Contained within the grid are nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, which must be located. Each region contains the digits 1 to 9 once each, such that no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions do not contain digits. Pink lines must contain a set of consecutive digits in any order, with no repeats. Cells on a pink line that are outside any regions, as noted above, do not therefore contribute towards that line's set. Circled cells indicate the number of cells from their respective region that that particular pink line passes through. For example, if r3c3 were 6, then its region would need to cover the entirety of that pink line. Any given pink line could contain no digits at all. Every circle contains a digit.

title: The Arithmetic Snake
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

We love snake puzzles and this is a cracker!  It's by Scruffamudda and involves a tiny bit of modulo arithmetic (!).  You can try "No '0' In Adder" at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BJ7MgMnT9f

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally the solver must find a single snake of orthogonally connected digits beginning at the given 1 which does not touch itself (even diagonally), does not touch any white dots but must visit each 3x3 box in the grid. Each digit on the snake is the sum of the previous two digits modulo 10 (eg 5+7 = 2). NB The second snake digit after the given 1 can be any digit. Grey digits are not on the snake but show the number of snake cells in the surrounding (up to) eight cells. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given.

title: A Blast of GAS
description:
Here is where you can try today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 306 – Secure Perimeter by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3ppuhk4p 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the indicated diagonals must sum to the total given (digits may repeat if allowed by other rules).
GAS 307 – Touchy Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/4d5wp4eb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every digit must be orthogonally adjacent to at least one other digit with a consecutive value. For instance, every 1 must touch at least one 2, and every 4 must touch at least one 3 or 5 (not necessarily both.)
GAS 308 – Diagonal Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/4jxdcmeh 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked diagonal must contain every number exactly once.
GAS 309 – The Vault by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/nfvhdnpz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line. (All lines are straight - they don't turn at intersections).
GAS 310 – David and Goliath by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p8fjzrm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage must contain one small digit and one large digit. The 'small' digit can be 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, and the 'large' digit can be 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9. (For instance, valid cages could include 2/5, 4/9, or 5/8. Cages like 2/3 or 7/9 are not allowed.)

title: The "Parity Mirror" Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Quick reminder that we're streaming the game Gorogoa tonight from 10pm UK time. We'd love to have your company if you can join us.

For today's puzzle, what would a sudoku addict see if they looked into the Mirror Of Erised?!  Well, ZegreS has come up with this gorgeous sudoku using a concept he calls the "Parity Mirror" so this could be the answer!  This has some really unusual logic and you can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gTQ3fMq6nM

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonal. The marked diagonal reflects odd/even parity on each side. (Eg if r6c2 is odd then r2c6 must also be odd.) Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits.

title: The Sudoku With Only 2 Given Digits
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
You've probably watched The Miracle Sudoku video but this one is, in its own way, just as extraordinary.  The same two given digits (a 1 and a 2) and a remarkably short ruleset... what is going on?  Try The Dutch Miracle from Aad van de Wetering at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hfpFTGNLrr

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each positive diagonal (ie from SW to NE): 1) all the digits are different; and 2) adjacent digits (ie those touching at a corner) must have a difference of at least 4.

Also, do check out this puzzle called The Aquarium by rubenscube which appeared on the channel earlier this week - it's a masterpiece.

title: ♥♥♥ The Digits Are Dating ♥♥♥
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's puzzle is (yet) another 100% sudoku from the mighty brain of zetamath... it's called Modern Romance and it turns out all of the digits 1-9 are dating :) Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bbR78tRnfd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits are dating. They have formed three couples and one throuple (a couple but with three people). The make-ups of these relationships are to be discovered. A heart between two cells indicates that the digits in those cells are in a relationship. ALL hearts are given. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits between the outermost members of the throuple in that row/column. eg If 123 are the digits in the throuple and the last row is 46 1(935)2 87 then the clue would be 17 (9+3+5).

Also, do check out this puzzle called The Aquarium by rubenscube which appeared on the channel earlier this week - it's a masterpiece.

title: Sudoku as an Olympic Event
description:
Here is where you can play Olympics by Civil: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hnMJTRhdrT Normal sudoku rules apply. All digits in the colored cells are part of at least one (summer) Olympic year. The years are depicted in orthogonally adjacent consecutive digits. Not all possible combinations within the colored area are depicting Olympic years. All digits joined by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. All possible black dots are given. 

Note: The Olympics began in 1896, and have occurred every four years since (excluding 1916, 1940 and 1944).

title: Time To Think Outside The Box
description:
*** WARNING ***
If you aren't sure about the riddle at the start of today's puzzle then you can use the second link below (which contains the puzzle with the solution to the riddle) and/or read the spoiler at the very base of this text.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today's puzzle is a very unusual one for the channel. It has a perfect rating on Logic Masters but, to solve the sudoku, you must first solve the riddle of why the lines are the shape they are in each of the 3x3 sudoku boxes!  The sudoku is by ZegreS and JeremyDover and it's absolutely gorgeous - if you can solve the riddle that is :)

 Give it a try at the link below: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rbjfJb33rn

To play the puzzle with box 5 REVEALED then use this link:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/H4mRDP3J26

Rules: 
There is a secret reason behind each shape in these sudoku boxes. The shape in box 5 is missing and solvers must fill in this shape to start. [If you can't work out this part, check the video description for a spoiler.] Normal sudoku rules apply. On gold "entropic" lines, every three adjacent digits consist of a low (1-3), medium (4-6) and high (7-9) digit. Each purple "renban" line connects a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits (which can appear in any order). Solvers must determine the type of line in box 5 (renban or entropic). title: Keeping the GAS Flowing
description:
Here are the URLs for today's puzzles:
GAS 301 – Region Sum Lines by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/35e4j9n6 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, there are some lines in the grid, and each line passes through more than one of the 3x3 regions. Along each line, the digits in every region it passes through have the same sum. For instance, r3c2 + r3c3 = r3c4 + r3c5.
GAS 302 – Odd/Even Killer by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/mv32hbkf 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in a cage must be different and add up to the number in the corner of the cage. Numbers in a grey circle must be odd. Numbers in a grey square must be even.
GAS 303 – Windoku of Opportunity by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2jx4mccy 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked 'window' region must contain each of the digits from 1 to 9 without repeats.
GAS 304 – Multiples of 3 by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3mf9udfu 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each of the 3x3 regions, every run of 3 vertically adjacent or 3 horizontally adjacent cells must sum to a multiple of 3. For instance, r2c123 must sum to a multiple of 3, r456c6 must sum to a multiple of 3, and so on.
GAS 305 – Odd/Even Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/k8uh2c6h 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in grey circles must be odd. Numbers in grey squares must be even.

title: The Yin And Yang Of Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
First things first - if you have any love of puzzles you must check out YESTERDAY'S sudoku - it's been getting a lot of attention on social media and with good reason: rubenscube has created a masterpiece.  Link here:

https://youtu.be/DUlfr6jmaNA

So today's puzzle has a lot to live up to but who better to do that than the mighty Phistomefel with his sudoku called Yin Yang Kropki Sudoku!  This is another magnificent hybrid of a classic logic problem and sudoku.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/92LftNNtD4

[Today's music intro is based on a chord progression I heard from the incredible Adrianne Lenker on the song Angels.]

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour the cells black and white such that the set of each colour is orthogonally connected and no 2x2 area is covered by only one colour. The given grey dots indicate that the two connected cells have the same colour. If a grey dot is between two black cells their digits are in a 1:2 ratio; if a grey dot is between two white cells, their digits are consecutive. ALL possible grey dots are given. [ie At the end of the puzzle, when all the cells are coloured and all the numbers are entered, two adjacent black cells may contain digits in a ratio of 1:2 only if there is a gray dot between them. Similarly, two adjacent white cells may contain consecutive numbers only if there is a grey dot between them. The following scenarios are possible without any problems: Two consecutive numbers in adjacent black cells; two digits in the ratio 1:2 in adjacent white cells; and any relationship between digits in adjacent cells with different colour.

There is an example puzzle available here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009P1
