title: Can ANYONE Solve This Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Mark sent Simon this sudoku - presumably as a prank.  It's called Progressive Divisors by DiMono and this is a something of a masterpiece.  But is it actually solvable?!!! Give it a try at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/progressivedivisors

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Progressive Divisor numbers are numbers where the first digit is divisible by 1, the first two digits taken as a two-digit number are divisible by 2, and so on. There is a nine digit Progressive Divisor number in row 1 of the grid, written from left to right. Each of the digits in row 1 is also in a distinct non-overlapping invisible region that sums to 3x the digit's value. These regions may branch, and digits may repeat in regions if allowed by other rules. The size and shape of these regions must be determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid indicate the first N cells in the row/column, read from outside-in, are a Progressive Divisor number, where N is the digit in the cell next to the clue. The cages hold two digit numbers that are either divisible by both digits (eg 24) or neither digit (eg 98).

title: GASson d'avril
description:
Here are the puzzles (including five Genuinely Approachable Sudoku puzzles) from this video:
GAS 296 – Palindrome Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/3zrs2h6h 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey lines must form a palindromic sequence; that is, they read the same from both directions.
GAS 297 – Chamber of Secrets by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p93mftm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given.
GAS 298 – Over 20 by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/msc5ua8t 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In every 3x3 region, there are three horizontally adjacent digits that sum to 20 or more, and there are also three vertically adjacent digits that sum to 20 or more.
GAS 299a – Skyscrapers by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/y8k9hdlm 
1-6 appear in each row and column. Treating each cell as a skyscraper of its digit’s height, a clue outside the grid indicates how many skyscrapers are visible in its row/column from its vantage point.
GAS 299b – Kakuro by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/ybntat35 
Each cell contains a digit between 1 and 9. Clues show the sum of the digits in the following group of white cells, which may not contain any repeats.
GAS 299c – Classy Sudoku by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3u8yvp3p 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 299d – Nonogram by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/ytaa6e66 
Shade some cells so that the clues outside the grid indicate the length of each connected group of black cells, in order, in the given row/column.
GAS 300 – Opheodrys by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/4wsut7nd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells directly connected by a green line must differ by at least 5.

title: Phistomefel's April Fool Puzzle!!
description:
In what must be one of the greatest April Fool pranks ever - even if only a few people and Cracking The Cryptic viewers will appreciate it, Phistomefel released the puzzle Simon attempts in this video on 1 April 2022.  Simon did not know it was released on April Fools Day when recording!!

You can play this remarkable puzzle which is called "♫ Slitherlink take me home ♫" here:

https://test.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qQt27GmmF2

Rules:
Draw two closed loops in the grid - a Touching Slitherlink that runs along the edges, and a Country Road that runs from cell centre to cell centre. Neither of the two loops may touch or cross themselves. Not all grid points have to be traversed by the Slitherlink and not all cells have to be visited by the Country Road. Each number is either a Touching Slitherlink clue or a Country Road clue. Both at the same time is also possible. A Touching Slitherlink clue indicates how often the loop touches the edges of the cell containing the clue. The Slitherlink divides the grid into several regions to which the Country Road clues refer. A Country Road clue indicates the number of cells visited by the Country Road in that region. The Country Road passes through each such region exactly once. Cells not visited by the Country Road may be orthogonally adjacent only if they are in the same area. Each region can contain none, one or more Touching Slitherlink clue(s), and each region can contain none or one Country Road clue(s). If a region contains no Country Road clue, an arbitrary number (greater than 0) can be traversed by the Country Road.

In the video, Simon first attempts a Country Road puzzle by Eric Fox to remind himself of the rules of Country Road!  You can play this puzzle here:

https://tinyurl.com/yzpwwppu

Rules:
Draw a non-intersecting loop through the centers of some cells which passes through each region exactly once. A number in a region represents how many cells in the region are visited by the loop. Orthogonally adjacent cells across a region border may not both be unused.

title: Are 10 Lines Or 11 Lines Used Here?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another brilliant sudoku from zetamath today - this one called 10 Lines.... (yet there are 11 lines in the grid!) Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/DMp47hdP2D

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap. Digits may repeat freely on lines and even within sums. For example, 23573 would be a valid fill for a length 5 line because we may divide it as 235 - 73.

description:
Here's where you can try today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 291 – Hi Mark! by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3dj8r73y 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in corner circles must appear in the surrounding four cells, in some order. Digits in cells separated by a V must sum to 5; digits in cells separated by an X must sum to 10. (No negative constraint - adjacent digits not separated by a letter can still sum to 5 or 10.)
GAS 292 – Star Product by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/y2nvjdj2  
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value outside of the grid gives the product of all highlighted digits in its row or column.

Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 294 – How I Set GAS by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/c6k2pefw  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along arrows must sum to the circled total.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, a clue outside of a row or column tells you some digits that must appear in the first three cells (nearest to the clue) in that row or column. For instance, row 2, columns 7-9 must contain a 4 and a 5.

title: Sudoku: The Chaos Construction
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A wonderful sequel to KNT's debut on the channel last week in the form of this Chaos Construction, called Killer.  This has a whole heap of wonderful logic in it. Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fqm7gDbF4j

Rules: 
Place one of each digit 1-9 in every row, column and region. The puzzle's nine regions must be determined by the solver and each consists of 9 orthogonally connected cells, which cannot overlap. Digits in a cage must sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage. Every cage is entirely contained within one region. ie for any cage, no two cells within that cage belong to different regions.

title: Sudoku goes into Orbit
description:
Here's where you can play Orbital Sandwiches 3 by Dusara: https://tinyurl.com/rzv6m9yw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Small circles / 'planets' are inside a 'sandwich'. A sandwich consists of a sum of digits enclosed by two buns; both a crown (9), and a heel (1). Digits may repeat within a sandwich, excluding the sandwich's two buns (9 and 1).

How cool is this grid!  Peter Veenis has come up with this beautiful rendition of the Easter Bunny in sudoku form!  Not only that but this is such a great puzzle to solve. Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/n7jmhb6HpN

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits (in any order). title: GAS Today - All my troubles seem so far away ...
description:
Here are the links for today's five Genuinely Approachable Sudoku puzzles:
GAS 286 – Multiplication by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3f8m36bj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each cage, read the two digits in the bottom two cells as a two-digit number from left to right. This number is the product of the two digits in the top two cells. Digits may repeat in a cage.
GAS 287 – XV Arrow Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2dss6kcf 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must add up to the number in the attached circle. Numbers separated by a V must add up to 5. Numbers separated by an X must add up to 10. Not all X's and V's are necessarily given.
GAS 288 – Dotted Lines by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/yw4cbrzz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive; digits in cells separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. Not all dots are given.
GAS 289 – Treasure Hunt by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3nknmtkz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a pink cell tells you how many of the (up to 8) adjacent cells contain digits strictly greater than itself. For instance, if a pink cell contains a 5, exactly 5 of the surrounding cells must contain digits that are higher than 5. 
GAS 290 – PointingDifferent by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/svvz52bv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each diagonal pointed at by an arrow contains the indicated number of distinct digits.

title: The 69 Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Despite our tongue-in-cheek title for this puzzle it must surely be one of the most beautiful sudokus ever constructed.  It is completely symmetrical - right down to the fact that, if you rotate the given 6 and 9 around 180° they become each other!! It's called If 6 was 9 and it's by Scruffamudda and you simply have to try this one!

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/DPnP3BnNng

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits within each cage must sum to either 6 or 9. By rotating the grid through 180° each cage sum is also rotated such that 6 becomes 9. For example, the cage at r1c234 must have a different value to the cage at r9c678. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are given.

title: The Phistomefel Movie
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
He's back!  With his normal dose of genius-infused mayhem, Phistomefel presents Loop Sum - a puzzle that is definitely difficult but also incredibly rewarding. Give it a try, you won't regret it.

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/ML8NMNhdGH

Rules: 
Fill the grid with the digits 1 to 9 such that every row, column and region contains each digit exactly once. The regions are sets of nine orthogonally connected cells and have to be determined by the solver. Draw a loop that travels horizontally and vertically from cell to cell. This loop enters and exits every region exactly once. A small clue in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits in all cells visited by the loop in that cell's region.

There is an example puzzle at the following link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009LJ

title: You Do The... MOTH?!?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A highly original offering today courtesy of Nahileon with their puzzle Just Do The Moth.  This is such a brilliant sudoku - it sounds impossible and yet... Quick reminder: You can draw loops in our software by enabling the Pen Tool.  (Click the cog icon next to the grid and turn Pen Tool on).

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/DHd3Fg3QTH

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw two closed loops in the grid that don't intersect themselves or each other. A loop travels horizontally or vertically between cell centres. Each loop must be situated entirely on one side of the highlighted diagonal and is a mirror image of the other with respect to that diagonal. A digit in a grey cell gives the number of cells in its row (or column, because of the symmetry) that are NOT part of either loop. Adjacent digits along either loop must have a difference of at least 5. 

There is also an example grid at the start of the video if the above is unclear.

title: This Sudoku Was Made By A Clown!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Three birthdays to celebrate today including that of the constructor Riffclown whose puzzle we attempt in the video!  It's called Whispered Somethings and it's a beautiful hybrid of two of our favourite rules.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hFRMdthhM3

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. All lines are both 'German Whispers' and Region Sum Lines! Digits on Region Sum Lines have an equal sum within each 3x3 box the line passes through. (Eg r6c6 = r5c7 + r4c7 = r7c5 + r7c4 = r8c3 + r9c2). Adjacent digits on German Whispers lines must have a difference of at least 5. In this puzzle, all lines must satisfy BOTH properties.

title: A Gassive Attack
description:
This video has been reloaded - with the obstructive advert amended! Here's where you can find today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles: 
GAS 281 – 22/7 Gas Edition by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/ync59rbs Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 282 – Quadruples by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p8897tt Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in circles must appear in one of the four cells around the circle. If a number appears more than once in a circle then it must appear at least that many times around it.
GAS 283 – Ordered Sums by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/32dm8cjk Normal sudoku rules apply. The cages are ranked from lowest to highest sum. Cages marked with a '1' have the lowest (not necessarily unique) total out of all of the cages in the grid, cages marked with a '2' have the second-lowest total, and so on. The totals are not necessarily consecutive. Cages with the same total may or may not contain the same set of digits.
GAS 284 – Lockout Lines by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/mr24hz3n Normal sudoku rules apply. Two connected diamonds must contain numbers with a difference of at least 4, and all digits on the line connecting them must lie strictly outside the range defined by those two numbers. For example, on a line whose diamonds contain 2 and 7, the only permissible numbers are 1, 8 and 9.
GAS 285 – GAS O’Clock by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2nh5etdk Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!

title: A Vision For Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for KNT and their puzzle Vision - which has a cool new ruleset that yields some beautiful logic.  Simon is a little hungover today so please be especially kind in your comments :)

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8JtTJL3JPQ

Rules: 
Place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and region. The regions must be determined by the solver. Each region is a set of nine orthogonally connected cells. If a digit N is in a circle then exactly the next N cells in the direction of the arrow (and only those N cells) are in the same region as that circle. eg if r6c5 was a 2 then r6c5, r5c6 and r4c7 would be in the same region and that region would not include r3c8 or r2c9.

description:
This is a collaboration by many setters from a stream. You can try it here: https://tinyurl.com/y9wbdmal 

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the value in the diamond. If the arrow is horizontal, then the digit in the diamond indicates where the column number of the diamond appears in the row, e.g. if r9c5 is a 7 then r9c7 is a 5. Similarly, if the arrow is vertical, then the digit in the diamond indicates where the row number of the diamond appears in the column, e.g. if r2c7 is a 5 then r5c7 is a 2. If a diamond has arrows in both directions then it follows both rules.

Some of you might remember the original Miracle Sudoku - a remarkable puzzle with just a couple of digits in the grid. title: Inspiring GAS
description:
Here are the links for today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles: 
GAS 276 – You Can’t Count on Us by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/yejwx73f Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 277 – Consecutive/LK by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/nhcee9ar Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal must sum to the value shown. Digits may repeat along a diagonal, as long as they follow sudoku rules. Digits on either side of a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given.
GAS 278 – XV Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/5n8fysev Normal sudoku rules apply. Two numbers separated by a 'V' must add to 5. Two numbers separated by an 'X' must add to 10. There is no negative constraint; that is, if two numbers do not have a symbol between them, they may still add to 5 or 10.
GAS 279 – Lickable Sudoku by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2s4an8kd Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in orthogonally adjacent cells cannot be consecutive.
GAS 280 – Stacking by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5cxxk372 Normal sudoku rules DO NOT apply! Enter the digits 1 through 6 ONLY into the grid, so that each row, column, and 3x3 region contains each digit once each. Some cells will be left blank. Also, every time two digits touch vertically, the digit on the bottom must be greater than the digit on the top.

title: One of the Most Dynamic Puzzles Ever
description:
Here's where you can play Dynamic Dots by Niverio: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/q4LqbrBR4b 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey dot represents one of the following 4 constraints: a White Dot connects two consecutive digits; a Black Dot connects two digits with a ratio of 1:2; a V connects two digits that sum to 5; an X connects two digits that sum to 10. If a cell is connected to different cells via multiple grey dots, each such grey dot must have a different property in terms of which constraint it represents. Every single grey dot represents exactly one constraint (eg 2 and 3 cannot be connected via a grey dot, since the grey dot would be a valid white dot and a valid V clue). Not all possible dots are given.

title: The 10x10 Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yes this grid seems the wrong size!  It's a 10x10 and we have to locate the regions within it!  This puzzle is called Smorg and it's by Jakhob and wooferzfg AND it's a chaos construction that is APPROACHABLE.  So do have a go if you have time, you can play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LjtD6LjLRF

Rules: 
Fill some cells in the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in a row or column and some cells are left empty. All empty cells in the grid must be orthogonally connected. All digits must belong to a region, which is an orthogonally connected group of 9 cells. Digits may not repeat in a region. Regions may not touch each other orthogonally. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits before the first empty cell seen from that direction. A digit in a circle indicates how many of the 8 surrounding cells are empty. A cell with a circle must contain a digit. Not all circles are necessarily given.

title: Do You Know Your Odd Numbers From Your Evens?!
description:
*** PATREON UPDATE ***
Today we released a new monthly reward set of puzzles!  Send us your solution by 20th April for a chance to win a prize!

Also Simon's solve of Phistomefel's latest puzzle: Slitherlink Liars  - which is a 100 minute video (!) is OUT!

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new constructor makes their debut today with a brand new - and very cool - ruleset.  You can play ExFalsoQuodlibet's Parity Lines here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qJt66F2JG4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line has two circles. One of these circles gives the total number of odd digits on the line, and the other circle gives the total number of even digits on the line. Both of these totals include the digits in the circles. For each line, the solver must determine which circle counts the even digits and which counts the odd digits. Digits may repeat along a line if allowed by the other rules. Digits in the cage sum to the given total.

Play it at the link below:

title: Normal Sudoku Rules MOSTLY Apply!?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Well, what can we say about this one... it's quite mad and utterly beguiling!  It's called Killer Shikoku and it's the work of the_cogito.  The rules completely flummox Simon but can you make sense of them? Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HtjrbnP8mt

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules mostly apply; however the grid contains no 5s. Instead every row, column and box has a single repeated digit. (NB Beware! This does NOT mean that you could find nine cells in which 5s could be placed to make a genuine grid!) Additionally: divide the grid into rectangular regions of orthogonally connected cells. Each rectangle contains exactly one circle. A single cell with a circle counts as a 1x1 rectangle. A number in a circle represents how many cells are in the rectangle the circle belongs to. Rectangles cannot overlap. Every cell in the grid is part of a rectangle. Digits may not repeat in a rectangle.

title: Everything Is Right(n)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're delighted to see the return of an old favourite to the channel today in the form of DiMono - the evil genius behind the puzzle Everything Is Wrogn, which we're sure many of you will remember! This puzzle is altogether easier but it's still very interesting.  It's called Snake Pit and you can give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/b9pPRJPRNL

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are "X-Snake sums". X-Snakes are basically bendy X-Sums: orthogonally connected 1-cell wide paths that begin in the cell next to the clue (the 'tail' cell). Snakes are X cells long, where X is the digit in the tail cell, and sum to the value of the clue without repeating any digits. Snakes may not touch themselves OR ANY OTHER SNAKE orthogonally. The snakes are racing to the grey rock in the centre of the pit (grid!). Exactly one cell of exactly one snake must touch the rock orthogonally or diagonally to win the race. (ie there is only ONE snake cell in box 5). Snakes don't eat rocks so neither the rock cell nor its digit may appear in any snake.

title: A GAS Trick
description:
Here's where yo ucan try today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 266 – Product Arrow by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/56xrhztd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along each arrow must MULTIPLY to give the product shown in the circle. 
GAS 267 – Rock Steady by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p9xr5fu 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells directly connected by a green line must differ by at least 5. 
GAS 268 – Killer Between by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/yjvkddzp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the value indicated. Digits along a line must have values between the values of the digits in the two circles on the ends of that line.
GAS 269 – Arrow Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/mwzdupxz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits placed on an arrow must add up to the total in the arrow's circle.
GAS 270 – Sudoku Make me a Sandwich by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p8znhx9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value outside of the grid is a sandwich clue: it tells you the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column, not including the 1 and 9 themselves.

title: A Puzzle For Mental Health
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Thrilled today to be able to share with you Thomas Snyder's latest sudoku which is called 3/25 (note the date!).  Thomas will be known to many of you as the man behind gmpuzzles.com and/or the three-time World Sudoku Champion and former World Puzzle Champion. description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very clever sudoku today that teaches you something you probably didn't know and/or realise!  The puzzle's called Downward Spiral and it's by a collection of setters calling themselves The Sudoku Skunkworks (!). We believe the 'skunkworks' is made up of Virtual, Sotek, XeonRisq, Bremster, Riffclown, and Eclectic Hoosier. Give it a try at the link below:

title: For My Friend Matthew: Ave Atque Vale
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another beautiful AND approachable sudoku today, this time courtesy of SSG with a puzzle titled Equals X. 

If you'll indulge me, I want to write a few words about my friend Matthew Slingo, who was taken from us far too soon.  I didn't trust myself to address this during the video but he was one of my very favourite people.  He was also so so encouraging when I came up with the idea of Cracking The Cryptic all those years ago on one of our many ski holidays.  His belief in the channel as a concept made me that much more certain it could succeed and it gave me the confidence to persevere with it in those early days.  For the last 20 years we have had some incredible trips to Europe and North America; picked each other up after many a wipe-out and set the world to rights on countless chair lifts. I will miss you buddy. RIP.

Play today's puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JpFrnGBRbd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order). Each main diagonal (marked in blue) cannot contain a repeated digit. The sum of the digits on an orange line within a single box must be the same for each box that line passes through. eg r2c5 + r2c6 = r3c7 = r4c8 + r5c8 + r6c8.

title: Another Session on the GAS
description:
Here are today's five puzzles:
GAS 261 – Kropnosis by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/yckwsv2x  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive; digits in cells separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. All dots may not be given.
GAS 262 – Rank Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p8p5zvs 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Each cage contains some gray numbers with # signs; these tell you the 'rank' of the value in that cell, compared to all of the other values in the cage. For instance, the digit in the #1 cell must be the lowest in its cage, the digit in the #2 cell must be the second lowest in its cage, etc. 
GAS 263 – Arrow Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p92fkfs 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must add up to the total in the adjoining circle.
GAS 264 – Thermoboros by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3yhpbz96 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase from bulb to tip.
GAS 265 – Box Battle by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/4aeyfhan 
Normal sudoku rules apply. At each border between two 3x3 regions, there are three pairs of digits straddling that border. If the inequality signs show that a region is greater than its neighbor, then that region has the greater digit in at least two out of the three pairs (but not necessarily all three pairs).

title: SAY The Clues To Solve The Puzzle!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A really beautiful and innovative sudoku today from Derektionary where you actually have to speak the clues to understand how they work!  It's called Look-and-Say Killer 2 and you can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pngjf2LGHq

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may repeat in cages and along indicated diagonals. Every given clue should be read as a "look-and-say" number. Each number says which digits are in the respective cage or on the respective diagonal. Eg if a cage clue is 1221, this means there is one 2 and two 1s in the cage. If a diagonal says 33 then there are three 3s along the diagonal.

title: Finding A Snake For St Patrick
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Another astonishing puzzle today, this time from Lizzy01 and her Snake In The City sudoku. This one is a marvellous "building-levelling snakezilla" as henrypijames on Logic Masters Germany commented! You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pr8b4tmLpL

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells to form a snake (a one-cell wide path that does not branch, cross itself or touch itself orthogonally. It can touch itself diagonally.) The snake consists entirely of odd digits and its head and tail are given by the grey circles. Clues outside the grid are skyscraper clues that ignore any snake cells in their row/column. ie Each digit that is not snake indicates the height of a building in that cell. Clues indicate the number of buildings that can be seen in their row/column from the side of the clue, where higher buildings obscure the view of lower buildings. Digits separated by an X sum to 10; digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all Xs and Vs are necessarily given.

title: Hitting the GAS Again
description:
Here are the five puzzles played today:
GAS 256 – Thermo Between by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2mbczamt 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase (not necessarily consecutively!) from the round bulb to the tip. The bulb of the leftmost thermometer is hiding behind the circle in r4c1... sorry! Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the two circles on the ends of the line. 
GAS 257 – Palindrome Quads by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p988dyj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers placed on a grey line must form a palindromic sequence; that is, they must read the same in both directions. The numbers appearing in a white circle must be placed somewhere in the four cells surrounding the circle.
GAS 258 – Pufferfish by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/35wu87xv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 259 – Number 5 is Alive by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p982wa7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to a value ending in 5, such as 5, 15, 25, etc.

title: Where Are The Arrows Hiding?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A really cool new idea emerges in today's sudoku which is called FourCast and it's by Nordy.  Each circle is meant to have an arrow and it's our job to work out where they go!  Do give the puzzle a try at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7qtdB7rFMB

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with grey squares must contain even digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle - except all arrows are hidden! Each circle has exactly one hidden arrow that is 3 cells long and extends from its circle in a straight line, either horizontally or vertically. Arrows may not cross, overlap or share cells with other arrows/circles.

Note that we've also shared The Sudokutown Murders by Nordy and Loric as a free post on our Patreon page.  If there's demand we'll record a video of this puzzle in due course.

title: A New Sudoku Theorem
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Aad van de Wetering returns to the channel today with a puzzle to demonstrate a new sudoku theorem!  The puzzle is called Theorema van Thoen - we think Thoen refers to Aad's friend and co-book-author Aad Thoen.  It's a very interesting sudoku indeed and you can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3bLj4rptT3

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The yellow line is a palindrome and must read the same backwards and forwards. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.

Thanks to Pim Shreurs for the music at the end of the video, which is called "The Maximum Of 5 Colors" and which we really like. Please note that Pim's Twitter handle is @sirxemic  (there is a typo in the outro text).

title: Natural GAS
description:
Here are the five (actually, eight!) URLs for today's GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 251 – Extra Regions by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2uxbf2b7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each shaded region must contain the digits from 1-9 exactly once each.
GAS 252 – XV by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p9cbhfs 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If an X appears between two digits, those two digits sum to 10. If a V appears between two digits, those two digits sum to 5. If a pair of digits isn't marked, you don't know anything about its sum.
GAS 253 – Heart in a Cage by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/ycy4y47d 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the total given.
GAS 254 – Kropki Pairs by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/mvckjbn4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all dots are given.
GAS 255 – Big3 Nonconsec by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/3wvpr6wy  
1-6 appears in each row, column and region. Digits in orthogonally adjacent cells cannot be consecutive.
Big3 Diagonal by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2r7wkc56 
1-6 appears in each row, column and region. The marked diagonals cannot contain repeated digits.
Big3 Antiknight by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p86zjw9 
1-6 appears in each row, column and region. Cells separated by a (chess) knight's move cannot contain the same digit.
Big3 Antiking by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/yc3yr3ad 
1-6 appears in each row, column and region. Cells separated by a (chess) king's move cannot contain the same digit.

title: Can You Draw A Simple Loop Through A Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dying Flutchman returns to the channel today with a simply brilliant hybrid puzzle where we need to solve a sudoku but also draw a simple loop... this might sound simple but is it?! Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/B4fMfpp3FG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a "simple loop" in the grid ie a single closed loop that visits all cells except the ones containing a 5. The loop must go horizontally or vertically from cell to cell without branching or intersecting itself. Grey-cell clues outside the grid give the sum of the all the cells between the border and the 5 in that row/column containing straight line segments. White-cell clues outside the grid give the sum of all cells between the border and the 5 in that row/column containing corner segments.

title: The Twisted Magic Square
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for Chris C and their puzzled Twisted Magic, which is an unusual sudoku based around the magic square!  This is a LOT of fun and you can play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/DMdfdnRGDf

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. title: That Doesn't Look Like A Thermo Sudoku!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
PulverizingPancake returns to the channel today with a wonderful hybrid of thermo and fillomino - hence the unusual layout in the video.  This is such a lovely puzzle and it even names itself using the thermos!!
Do give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

CtC link: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/T63Gh3Rp9T

Penpa link: https://tinyurl.com/y8boyu75

Rules: 
Each cell is part of a region of N cells (N can be 1 or higher).  Regions of the same size can touch each other diagonally but not orthogonally. Cells on thermometers are in regions of strictly increasing size, starting from the bulb end (e.g. if the bulb is in a 2-cell region, the next cell along the thermo is in a region of at least 3 cells).

title: Hitting the GAS
description:
GAS 246 – Bullseye by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2p8bkr86 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along arrows must sum to the circled total.
GAS 247 – One by One by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3cbsjf4n 
Fill the grid with the numbers 1 through 5 only, so that each digit appears exactly once in each row, column, and 3x3 region. (Some cells will remain empty!). Also, each gray line has exactly one cell containing a digit. 
GAS 248 – Odd/Even Renban by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/ynhn8pwh  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a pink line must form a set of consecutive digits, but in any order. Digits in a grey circle must be odd. Digits in a grey square must be even.

title: The Puzzle They Said We Should Never Do...
description:
*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***
Today we feature a puzzle that our testers were a bit worried about.  It has quite a complicated ruleset and this leads to much head-scratching but it's worth it!!  It's called Bicycles and it's by SirSchmoopy making his debut on the channel! Do give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rRJ2Tq4b6f

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Along a thermometer digits increase from the bulb end. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Within a row, let a "cycle" be the path taken starting from digit A in column X and then looking at digit B in Column A, then digit C in Column B etc until the cycle returns to digit A again. The "order" of a cycle is the number of unique digits contained in the cycle. eg A 5 in r9c1, a 9 in r9c5 and a 1 in r9c9 would force a cycle of order 3. In this puzzle the ORDER of the CYCLES also increases along thermometers starting from the bulb end. 

Apparently this puzzle uses a mathematical concept, which is explained further here:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclic_group

*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***
A challenging but fascinating puzzle today from PjotrV (Peter Veenis).  It's called Hawaii and it's a spiral galaxy/sudoku hybrid that's been lauded by the likes of Phistomefel. Do give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fJnrmHf8QT

Rules: 
In each row and column the digits 1-9 must appear exactly once. Each cell is part of a “galaxy”. There are big galaxies of exactly 9 cells and island galaxies which are smaller than 9 cells. Digits can't repeat in galaxies. Each galaxy is 180 degrees rotational symmetric. In the centre of each galaxy there is exactly one circle either between 2 cells or in a cell. A circle in a cell is odd and a circle between 2 cells is a consecutive pair. Some of the circles are given, the other circles must be deduced (but all circles must have the circle properties listed above). Island galaxies can't touch each other, not even diagonally. Clues outside the grid sum the digits of the island galaxies in that row or column.

There is also an example puzzle available to play here:
https://tinyurl.com/368xtmcm

And the solution can be checked here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=00091U

title: Donning the GAS Mantle
description:
Here are the URLs for today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 241 – Pole Position by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/b8p72yp7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The leftmost digit in each row tells you the location of the digit 1 in that row (for instance, if the leftmost digit is a 4, then the 1 in that row is in the 4th column). The topmost digit in each column tells you the location of the digit 1 in that column.
GAS 242 – Classic Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2d4pjspr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 243 – Multiple Man by Philip: https://bit.ly/3glOsVo 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue regions are clones, and must contain the same digits in the same relative positions.  
GAS 244 – Killer Between by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/542nzek6 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the value indicated. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line. For instance, if the circles on the ends of a line contain the digits 4 and 8, the digits along the line can only be 5, 6, or 7. Digits along a line can repeat. 
GAS 245 – Outside Parity by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/rrbebjn5 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid tells you how many of the first digits in that row or column are either all odd or all even, before the first change. For example, a clue of 3 tells you that either the first 3 numbers are odd and the 4th is even, or vice versa.

title: The Miracle "Windowed" Sudoku
description:

Craziness today courtesy of Nahileon and their puzzle Isolation.  At first glance this looks unsolvable (and at second glance it still looks mighty difficult!).  BUT this IS a MASTERPIECE. Do give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QpMDNMDFQq

title: Paranormal Sudoku Rules Apply
description:
Heres' where you can play Suguru Chaos Deconstruction by Math Pesto: https://tinyurl.com/yxkz85wk 
Fill some cells in the grid with the digits 1–9 such that no digit repeats in a row or column. Cells containing a circle, square, or arrow must have a digit in them. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the circle. Gray squares contain even digits and gray circles contain odd digits. A region is a collection of orthogonally connected cells. A region of size n contains the digits 1 through n once each. Regions may not touch each other orthogonally, although they may touch each other diagonally.

title: A Puzzle To Celebrate 450,000 Subscribers
description:
*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***

A huge Thank You to WombatBreath for sending us this super sudoku to celebrate Cracking The Cryptic reaching 450,000 subscribers.  Who would have thought that our little channel where we admire the logic the wonderful constructors pour into their puzzles could have tempted so many of you to regularly visit us.  Do give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

Colourful version:
https://tinyurl.com/ycxevrkd

Black and white version (which Simon uses in the video):
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gN79Qm9HfT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages or on the ampersand (which therefore forms an additional region). All cages contain digits summing to the same total, which is to be determined. Letters represent the digits 1-9 in alphabetical order (so A=1, E=2, ..., R = 9). Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given.

title: Sudoku Through the Looking Glass
description:
Here's where you can try Through the Looking Glass by Cam: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rg6ptPrtBF 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats. Each digit (1-9) has a "buddy" that appears in all of the cells where the row and column indices are swapped. For example, if 1's are buddies with 4's and there is a 1 in r5c2, then there must be a 4 in r2c5. A number may be its own buddy. Figuring out the buddies is part of the puzzle.

title: Mission Impossible:  Sudoku Edition
description:
*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***
After Simon solved a relatively straightforward puzzle yesterday, he gets his comeuppance today taking on Frak by zetamath.  This is a VERY interesting (and challenging) sudoku.  It has a perfect 100% rating on Logic Masters Germany but also merits its highest difficulty rating.  Do give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8DfMHmLpqP

Rules: 
Place the digits 1 to 9 once each into each row, column and region.  Regions need to be deduced by the solver and consist of 9 orthogonally-connected cells. For each blue line, digits on the line have an equal sum N within each region the line passes through. If a line passes through the same region more than once, each individual segment of such a line within that region sums to N separately. Every line must enter at least two regions. A digit in a circle indicates the number of digits on that particular segment of the line within that region. Not all circles are necessarily given.

PS Our cryptic clue on Twitter to this puzzle was:

Once played on the BBC, candid cameraman finally quits?

which is FRANK (candid) - N (final letter of cameraman) and refers to the BBC Micro 1984 game FRAK, which Simon mentions in the video.

title: Another stop for GAS
description:
Here are today's five URLs for playing these Genuinely Approachable SUdoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 236 – Consec Pairs by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p8w9ct5
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits which are separated by a white dot must be consecutive.
GAS 237 – Morph by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/6kvtbxcr
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. There is no negative constraint (i.e. if two digits are not separated by a dot, then they may or may not be consecutive).
GAS 238 – Battenburg by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p8hmym6
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every time a blue square appears at the intersection of four cells, the odd and even digits in those four cells must be in a 'checkerboard' pattern (two odd digits diagonally opposite each other, and two even digits diagonally opposite each other). Every time a white square appears at an intersection of four cells, the odd and even digits in those four cells must NOT be in a 'checkerboard' pattern. 
GAS 239 – Diagonal Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p8v578u
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked diagonal must contain the numbers 1-9 exactly once.
GAS 240 – Punisher by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/2dzys2mj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given. Digits along the indicated diagonals must sum to the total given (digits may repeat if allowed by other rules).

title: A Perfect Sudoku Puzzle
description:
*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***
Simon is still on his laptop today - we hope the sound quality is ok.  Today's sudoku is one we'll remember for a long time.  It's called LITS Killer and it's by AFrayedKnot.  It's just a beautiful hybrid of the logic puzzle LITS and Killer Sudoku.  Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fLbtDgFRhm

Rules: 
Fill every row, column and bold-outlined region with the digits 1-9 once each. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Shade one tetromino in each region such that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Tetrominoes of the same shape may not share a border (counting rotations and reflections as the same). No 2x2 area may be entirely shaded. Additionally, each tetromino must contain digits summing to less than 13.

title: The Cleverest Dot-To-Dot Puzzle Ever
description:
*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***
Today's sudoku, which must surely be the cleverest (and hardest!) dot-to-dot puzzle ever was created by Jay Dyer.  Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QH26FPT6mF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along 'box-sum lines', digits on the line have the same sum within each 3x3 box the line passes through. The lines must be determined by the solver. All ends of lines are marked with grey dots. Lines can only move orthogonally (ie never diagonally), cannot touch themselves orthogonally, cannot branch and cannot cross themselves or other lines. title: Squaring The Circles
description:
*** TODAY'S SUDOKU ***
We're delighted to be to share the brand new Qodec puzzle with you:  Ship's Wheel.  This is a hybrid of sudoku and the Japanese logic puzzle Shikaku and it's ridiculously clever.  Just a few symmetrical circles is all Qodec needs to make a masterpiece.  Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QbR6pNt3jh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each main diagonal (marked in blue) cannot contain a repeated digit. Divide the grid into rectangular regions of orthogonally connected cells. A square is a form of rectangle. Each rectangle contains exactly one circle.  A number in a circle represents how many cells are in the rectangle the circle belongs to. Rectangles cannot overlap. Every cell in the grid is part of a rectangle. Digits may repeat in a rectangle if allowed by other rules.

title: Cracking The Cryptic: The Extended Cut
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's video is a movie-length edition.  Simon does battle with Emre Kolotoglu's Border Sums - a chaos construction with a brand new ruleset and a perfect 100% rating on Logic Masters Germany. This is an extraordinary sudoku and you can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/G8r4LHFFBd

Rules: 
Each row, column, and region must contain the digits from 1 to 9 exactly once. The regions must be orthogonally connected and determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the two digits separated by the first region border seen from that direction in that row/column. (A row or column with a clue cannot be occupied by a single region.) For example; if the regions were the regular 3x3 boxes, then the clue at the top of column 6 would be the sum of R3C6 and R4C6, and the clue at the bottom of column 6 would be the sum of R6C6 and R7C6.

title: Laughing GAS
description:
Here are the URL's for today's FIVE genuinely approachable sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 226 – Corner/Edge by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/9fx3h93y 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A set of digits near a 3x3 region of the grid gives you some information about the digits in either the four corner cells or the four edge cells of that region. For instance, 'E 56' next to the middle-left region tells you that 5 and 6 appear in two of the four edge cells of that region (r4c2, r5c1, r5c3, or r6c2.)  Note: 'corner cells' and 'edge cells' refer to the four corner cells and four edge cells of the 3x3 sudoku region itself, which are not necessarily on the corners or edges of the whole grid.
GAS 227 – Arrow Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p8vww8t 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow must add up to the digit in the attached circle.
GAS 228 – Ernst by Philip: https://tinyurl.com/23cscfwa 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along green lines, digits must differ by at least 5.
GAS 229 – Bust Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2s3sxcbh 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value outside of a row or column tells you the position where that row or column 'goes bust'. If you sum the leftmost (or topmost) N digits in a row or column, the value outside of the row or column tells you the smallest possible value of N for which the sum is GREATER THAN 21. For instance, suppose that a row contains 3 8 4 6 9 2 5 1 7. If you sum just the first digit, the sum is 3. If you sum the first 2 digits, the sum is 11. If you sum the first 3 digits, the sum is 15. If you sum the first 4 digits, the sum is 21. If you sum the first 5 digits, the sum is 30. Since 30 is the first sum to be greater than 21, the clue outside of this row would be '5'.
GAS 230 – by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/2p892h2x 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey region contains the numbers from 1 to 9, and both grey regions contain exactly the same numbers in the same positions.

title: For the Love of Sudoku!
description:
Here's where you can try Three Hearts by James Kopp: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mgrb2BqHqr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the arrow's circle. Two of the orange dots are thermometer bulbs and the third is the beginning of a palindrome. Which dot is which is to be determined. The palindrome is 10 digits long and goes around one of the heart shapes. Numbers increase from the bulbs of the thermometers on both sides of the heart shapes to the common end point at the base of the heart (r5c3 and/or r9c3 and/or r7c7).

title: An Introduction To Variant Sudoku: Puzzle 2
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Many of our viewers have noted that it would be a good idea if, occasionally, we aimed videos explicitly at newcomers to the channel to try and showcase the world of variant sudokus in an accessible way.  This is the second puzzle in our Introduction To Variant Sudoku series.  It's a Sequence Sudoku by Thomas Fink from the 8th annual German Sudoku Championship qualifier, which took place last weekend (link below).  

We should stress that we are NOT saying this is an easy puzzle.  But it should be a puzzle that retains all the beautiful logic you'd expect to see in a sudoku on the channel whilst not being overwhelmingly complicated.  Play the puzzle at the link below:

title: 4 Minutes 33 Seconds:  Can You Solve It That Fast?
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today marks a debut on the channel for ndsurgenor with an exceptionally good (and minimalistic) puzzle dedicated to John Cage's unusual piece of music 4'33''.  You can listen to a seminal performance of this work here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ

Anyone who can solve this puzzle in 4 minutes 33 seconds is doing rather well.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4N3ThH99qg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply to the first 9 rows ie the 9x9 grid - but not the 10th row. The 10th row consists of all digits 1 to 9 once each and does not affect the 9x9 grid by sudoku; rather, a digit in this row indicates that the same digit is found in the equivalently valued row of that particular column. eg the digit 4 placed in row 10 means that 4 is found in the 4th row of that same column. Cages (which include the large red cage) must sum to either 3, 4, 33, 43 or 433; cages within the 9x9 grid may not contain repeated digits. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits; not all dots are given.

title: The Puzzle In A Puzzle In A Puzzle In A Puzzle In A Puzzle
description:
*** A Bonus Video***

As requested, Simon has a go at Inception by Matyas Martinka, surely one of the most incredible constructions in puzzle history.  You solve the first grid as a Hitori, then an Akari, then a Nurikabe, then a Killer Sudoku and then a Star Battle.  And every single puzzle is good!!  You can play it at the link below: 

https://tinyurl.com/inceptionpuzzle

Rules: 
All rules are standard and the individual puzzles are meant to be solvable even if you've never tried the given variant.

- Shade the grid by standard Hitori rules using the pencil marks as clues.
- Use the shaded cells' pencil marks as clues to shade the grid by standard Akari rules. If a shaded cell contains a pencil mark greater than 4, it acts as a 0 for Akari.
- If a cell contains a light bulb and it's corner mark is not 8 or 9, its pencil mark can be placed in the grid as part of the solution.
- Shade the grid by standard Nurikabe rules using the placed numbers as clues. (The pencil marks on shaded "water" Nurikabe cells are no longer needed.)
- Solve the grid as a standard Killer Sudoku where the cages are the Nurikabe islands, and the sum of the digits in the cage equals to the sum of the corner pencil marks in that cage. (The previously placed numbers remain in the grid.)
- In the solved Killer Sudoku, place 2 stars in every row, column and 3 by 3 region according to standard Star Battle rules. Cells with 4 or 5 must not contain stars.

Please note there is a full explanation of the rules at the link below:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000912

title: How To Solve Dave Gorman's New Cryptic Crossword
description:
*** Today's Crossword ***

It's been too long since we did a crossword on the channel and we're delighted to attempt a puzzle from British comedian/cruciverbalist Dave Gorman, which appeared in The Independent on 7 Feb 2022. Try the puzzle at the link below: 

https://puzzles.independent.co.uk/games/cryptic-crossword-independent

Puzzle number 11020 by Bluth (Dave's pseudonym).

A couple of comments on two of the clues (SPOILER ALERT):

1 Demeanour of experts circulating mails to support admission of guilt for covering up deception

I figured out exactly how this worked after I turned the webcam off.  "For covering up deception" is saying replace CON (deception) with PRO (for).  Very clever.

2 Bowler moving lower, looking up 10 across

There might be a slight inaccuracy here, which Dave was kind enough to mention to me.  A LOWER is a cow, for example ie a creature that LOWS.  So MOO as a synomym for LOWER may be a stretch as the dictionary doesn't support LOWER = LOW.

*** Today's Sudoku ***

Many of our viewers have noted that it would be a good idea if, occasionally, we aimed videos explicitly at newcomers to the channel to try and showcase the world of variant sudokus in an accessible way.  We intend to try and do this over the coming weeks starting with this puzzle called Parity Arrows by Testarossa.  

We should stress that we don't think this is an easy puzzle - or even a GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku).  It will require some careful thought but we do feel this puzzle is retains all the beautiful logic you'd expect to see in a sudoku on the channel whilst not being overwhelmingly complicated :)  

Try the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TbMnngP7GJ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits in circles also show the total number of cells of the same even/odd parity that that cell sees horizontally and vertically (including itself) before it hits a cell with another parity.

title: The Anti-Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

After yesterday's puzzle (see more on that below) which contained almost no information in the grid, today's puzzle looks like the setter has been VERY generous - what's going on?!  This is a VERY clever sudoku from Marvin Kannhäuser called Medley - it's the quintessential anti-miracle sudoku! Try the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/R4pBr43gb4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages add up to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage, if given. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The main diagonal (in blue) must include the digits from 1 to 9 once each. Digits within the white circles must appear at least once in the four cells touching the circle. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. The two digits on the two-cell-palindrome grey line must be the same. The cell with the grey square must contain an even digit. Cells separated by an X must contain digits that sum to 10. Black dots separate cells containing digits with a ratio of 1:2. White dots separate cells containing consecutive digits.

title: GAS Mark 5
description:
This video appeared briefly yesterday with a puzzle that could have been interpreted as an unfortunate symbol. This version shows roughly how Mark's solve went on a symbol-free version of the puzzle grid. Here are the URLs for today's 5 Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 216 – Small Samurai by Tyrgannus: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GLFmHPbrmh 
 In each of the 5 4x4 grids, 1-4 must be placed in each row, column and 2x2 region. Digits along the between line must have values between those of the ends of the line. Digits joined by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio; digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the circle. Digits along a thermo must increase from the bulb. 
GAS 217 – Slot Machine by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/mp9tvd6t 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each vertical strip has its digits in the same order. Digits wrap around when they reach the bottom of the grid.
GAS 218 – Thermo Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/2p8swf26 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers on a thermometer must strictly increase, starting from the bulb.
GAS 219 – Ego by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/2davrb6d 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in grey squares must be even. 
GAS 220 – Arrow Quads by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/4sd2rth5
Digits along an arrow must sum to the value in the attached circle. Digits in a white circle must appear somewhere in the four cells surrounding that circle. Note that if a digit appears twice in a white circle, it must appear at least twice in the four surrounding cells.

title: The Colourful Arrows
description:

Another day, another brand new ruleset!  Today we get to try vidarino's Corridors which, it turns out, is a very beautiful puzzle indeed! Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MTTm2LtHRG

Rules: 
The digits 1 to 9 must appear once each in every row, column and region. A region is an orthogonally connected set of nine cells and must be determined. A region cannot contain a 2x2 block of cells. title: Englishman Takes American Math Exam
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Tonight sees the return of an old favourite to the channel in the form of the American math(s) teacher, RockyRoer.  This puzzle (called Line Of Sight) is highly original and will test your brain's understanding of factors! Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LGLRMdDTMt

Rules: 
Fill each row, column and 7-cell region with the digits 1-7 once each. The boundaries of the regions must be determined. Clues in the grid indicate some of the cells that can see at least two cells in its same region both horizontally and vertically. Every digit it sees horizontally ((including itself) is summed and every digit it sees vertically (including itself) is summed and these sums have been multiplied together to give the clue. Region boundaries stop the line of sight. eg A cell with a value of 49 must be a product of 7*7, so the cell containing that clue must be able to be part of a sum horizontally to 7 as well as vertically.  So the cell could contain a 4 and have a 3 next to it horizontally; while it could have a 1&2 above and/or below it. Eg2 A cell with a value of 12 is the smallest clue possible and could be made a 1/2 in one direction and a 1/3 in the other direction.

PLEASE CHECK THE LINK BELOW IF YOU ARE IN ANY DOUBT OVER THE RULES AS THERE IS A USEFUL EXAMPLE:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0008YP

title: Try our New GAS Suppliers
description:
Here's where you can try our five new GAS constructors' puzzles:
GAS 211 – Kropki Pairs by Tyrgannus: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BMm4LGNQ7M
Normal Sudoku rules apply. A black dot between cells indicates cell values with a 2:1 ratio. A white dot between cells indicates cells with consecutive values. Not all dots are shown. 
GAS 212 – Search Nine by Freddie Hand: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/r84n6GgQfd 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in arrow cells indicate how far it is to the digit 9 in that direction. For example, if the digit 2 appears in r1c3, then a 9 must appear two cells to its right, in r1c5.
GAS 213 – XV Sudoku by Eric Fox: https://tinyurl.com/msw68sfp
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every pair of orthogonally adjacent cells which sum to 10 are marked with an X. Every pair of orthogonally adjacent cells which sum to 5 are marked with an V.
GAS 214 – Coordinate Sudoku by Shye: https://tinyurl.com/y8u94mnk
Normal Sudoku rules apply. The digits X, Y and Z in pill shapes (reading left to right) signify that rXcY = Z. For example, if a pill read [382], then the cell in row 3 and column 8 would have to be the digit 2. 
GAS 215 – Doubling Lines Sudoku by jovi_al: https://tinyurl.com/5d6mx8ut
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every digit that appears along a gray line must appear exactly twice on that line.

title: Snakes On A KLM Plane
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's puzzle is a great way to improve your mood...  Especially if your friend Pencil Mark has, in a spirit of pure evil, recorded his solve of the NEW Phistomefel puzzle before you even knew it existed!!!  [If you want to see Mark's solve of Sequence Sudoku then you can watch it on Patreon (link below)]  Dying Flutchman's German Hisses is this video's puzzle and some of the logic hidden within it is pure magic.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fdBbF4dTDF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are two snakes in the grid, the endpoints of which are given (as circles). Snakes cannot touch themselves or each other orthogonally but they can touch diagonally. Adjacent digits along a snake must differ by at least 5. The non-snake cells form several regions. In regions, digits cannot repeat. Some region totals have been indicated by small corner clues. The given digits indicate the number of snake cells within the 3x3 square centered on that digit.

title: Normal Sudoku SIZE Does Not Apply
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Wait... that's not a normal looking sudoku!  Indeed not... Jay Dyer returns to the channel with an 11x11 grid into which we need to locate the nine 3x3 regions we'd normally expect to see.  This is a puzzle that is great fun (and quite approachable).  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jqQHm9B29j

Rules: 
Contained within the grid are nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, which must be located. Each region contains the digits 1 to 9 once each such that no digit repeats in any row or column of the grid. Cells outside regions do not contain digits.  The digits in each cage sum to the clue in the top left corner, and may not repeat. Cages may include cells outside regions.

title: Balance Loop Sudoku - An Addendum
description:
*** Last Night's Sudoku ***

Last night we released an epic 2hr 15min video in which Simon did battle with the mighty Gliperal's Balance Loop Sudoku.  Some of the comments on that video noted that Simon had failed to explain a piece of the loop segment in column 1.  Let's put that right!

Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LdgRt8ddjQ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single closed loop that travels orthogonally through the centres of some cells. The loop does not use any cell more than once and must travel through each dot. The two loop segments extending from both sides of a dot must be balanced ie the sum of the digits up to and including the digit in the cell containing the first turn must be the same. ALL possible dots are given.

title: A Math Celebration
description:
Here's where to play Japanese Sums with Arrows by Math Pesto: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/B2nt9qTFp9 
Within the main 9x9 grid, normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the circle. Shade cells within the main 9x9 grid so that the clues outside the grid in order equal the sums of the digits in contiguous blocks of shaded cells in that row/column. Blocks must be separated by at least one unshaded cell. 
Note: The number of clues for a particular row/column is exactly the number of white cells outside the grid for that row/column. (For example, column 7 has three white cells outside the grid, so there are exactly three clues for column 7.) Also, numbers outside the main 9x9 grid don't have to adhere to normal sudoku rules: they can be greater than 9 (including in an arrow's circle), and can repeat in the row/column, etc.

title: Wordle: The Sudoku Version!
description:
*** Bonus Patreon Video ***

Simon takes on Phistomefel's new puzzle Fillomino Aquarium - which is one of the best puzzles we've ever seen.  Available now for our patrons over on Patreon at the link below.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's puzzle features a sudoku version of the internet sensation #Wordle - which has been clogging up our Twitter feed for the last two weeks. It's by a constructor with an unpronounceable name: Wooferzfg and it's called Siren Octal Dumpy for reasons that will be clear if you watched our YouTube short about Wordle :) Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fPB7jpgLm8

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There is a secret five digit number.  The coloured cells in a row, read left to right as a five digit number, represent a guess at the secret number. If a cell is green, that digit is in the secret number and in the correct position; if a cell is yellow, that digit is in the secret number but in the wrong position; if a cell is grey, that digit is not in the secret number. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  Not all dots are given.

title: Jumping Jack Flash, It's a Gas, gas, GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for today's five Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 201 – Thermwhich by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/3xxaw4fe 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase, starting from the round bulb. A value outside of the grid is a sandwich clue: it tells you the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column. 
GAS 202 – Christmas Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/2p8bmphb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line that connects two circles must all be different, and must be strictly less than the digits in both circles.
GAS 203 – Inferno by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/3vzesjhy 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase from bulb to tip.
GAS 204 – Lockout Lines by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/2p8jmd4x 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in diamonds joined by a line differ by at least 4 (for instance, 4 and 8, or 1 and 7), and all digits on the connecting line must be either higher than the larger diamond value, or lower than the smaller diamond value. The same line may contain a mixture of both higher and lower digits. Digits on a line may include repeats and may have no particular order.
GAS 205 – Small-scale Samurai by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/68NtD2Q6B7 
The grid consists of two overlapping 6x6 sudokus, each containing 1-6 in each row, column and 2x3 box. The digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle.

title: Keep Solving And Nobody Explodes
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Zetamath has been inspired by watching us explode in our recent livestreams...  and he's made a sudoku that proves to be one of the most interesting and difficult that we've ever seen.  A word of warning:  if you attempt this puzzle make sure you give yourself some time.  It will probably take you longer than 5 minutes.  Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Lt8N8ThFTM

Rules: 
Don't panic. There are several bombs hidden throughout the grid, but if you just follow these simple not at all convoluted directions you can disarm the bombs and save everyone. The bombs take the form of three regular sudoku digits which you must determine. All instances of each of those digits in the grid are bombs. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Therre are nine regions to be discovered, each containing nine orthogonally connected cells. The arrows point to bombs within the same region. The digit on the arrow tells you how many cells to travel to reach that bomb.  For example, if r6c2 is 3, that would tell you that r3c2 is a bomb digit in the same region as r6c2. Not all arrows are necessarily given. The black dots in the grid separate digits with a ratio of 1:2 which are in different regions. All such black dots are given. [Digits with a ratio of 1:2 that are in the same region are not marked.]

title: Phistomefel's Wall
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Simon takes on the latest masterpiece from Phistomefel, Wall Sudoku.  This is everything you'd expect: brilliant, original and brutal!!  Can you solve it!? Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/j87R9nmNNP

Rules: 
Each row, column and white or grey 3x3 box contains each digit 1 to 9 exactly once. Place a wall between all orthogonally adjacent cells that contain consecutive digits. Some walls are already given and they also separate two consecutive digits. A circled digit indicates how many cells it can see in a horizontal and vertical direction including its own cell. Walls obstruct the view. Not necessarily all circles are given.

To solve using the "wall drawing" interface Simon uses in the video, click the cog icon on the puzzle screen and select the option "Enable Pen Tool".  You'll then find an extra icon pops up that allows the drawing of all these extras :)

title: Rare Pencil Puzzles
description:
Simon tackles some more of the Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzle series from our Discord server!

Herugolf by Tyrgannus

Rules: Move the circles vertically or horizontally at least once each so that each circle ends up stopping on an H (hole). A ball can go in an H with potential moves still available as long as it lands at the end of a full move. A circle’s first move must be in a straight line of the number of cells indicated by the number inside it, and each successive move must be one cell shorter than the previous. Circles’ paths may not cross themselves, each other, other circles, or other circles’ starting points. They also may not pass over an H without stopping on it, and may not ever stop on a cell with water but can pass over it.

https://tinyurl.com/3a5bwjft

Cojun by Freddie Hand
Rules: Place a number into each cell so that each region contains the numbers from 1 to N with no repeats, where N is the number of cells in the region. Numbers of the same value may not touch  one another orthogonally. Where two numbers within a region are stacked vertically, the number on top must always be larger.

https://tinyurl.com/2hx8ubu9

U-Turns by Eric Fox
Rules: Draw a non-intersecting path through the centers of some cells which passes through every white circle and no black circles. Grey circles mark the ends of the path. Between each pair of circles the path uses, the path must turn exactly twice, and both turns must be in the same direction.

https://tinyurl.com/48wx9su7

Vama by shye
Rules: Shade some cells such that every row, column, and outlined region contains exactly 2 shaded cells, and all shaded cells in the grid form one connected network, orthogonally or diagonally.

https://tinyurl.com/dawcxs85

Ring Ring by jovi_al
Rules: Draw rectangular loops through the centers of empty cells so that every empty cell gets used. The sides of different rectangles may intersect each other, but not turn at their intersection or otherwise overlap.

https://tinyurl.com/2p8zvfpk

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TjdNrDhjd8

title: If You Think I'm Odd, Wait Until You See This!
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today is Christoph Seeliger day on CtC!  We have two related puzzles for you - both of which are supposed to be awesome.  Simon faces a very ODD sudoku in the form of Frank Spencer (apologies to Christoph who didn't give the puzzle a name!). That this sudoku can exist is pretty extraordinary but how does one actually solve it?! Play the puzzle at the link below:

title: The Most Requested Puzzle Ever
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's puzzle is basically brand new and yet we've had more recommendations to try it than just about any sudoku ever.  It's by Abed Hawila and it's some sort of hybrid between a Canal View logic puzzle (no, we didn't know what that was!) and a sudoku.  Oh and it's absolutely incredible. Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/m23L8jF87m

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Arrow circles are the clues for a “Canal View” puzzle. Ie These clues cannot be shaded, and represent the number of shaded cells connected in a straight line horizontally or vertically to the clue. No 2x2 region may be entirely shaded. Additionally, digits cannot repeat within unshaded regions.

You can find an example puzzle here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0008QY

title: Schrödinger's Cat Has 0 to 9 Lives!
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Regular viewers will be aware of Simon's assertion that there is no such thing as a Schrödinger cell....  starwarigami makes a mockery of this with a sudoku called Schrödinger's Killer!  This is really witty and innovative and James Bond might even make an appearance (!). Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hJ3qL9nN4Q

Rules: 
Place the digits 0-9 in the grid so that every row, column and 3x3 box contains every digit exactly once. To enable this, there is a single Schrödinger cell in each box, containing a superposition of two different digits. Every Schrödinger cell contains a unique pair of digits. No Schrödinger cell can see another Schrödinger cell by a Queen's move in chess (i.e. any distance horizontally, vertically or diagonally). Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the indicated total. Schrödinger cells contribute the average of their two digits to the cage total.

title: The Friendly Snake that doesn't Touch Itself
description:
Here's where you can try Snek is Friend by Philip Newman: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6b4fM2jNL4  Normal sudoku rules apply. All friendly cells in the grid form a single one-cell-wide orthogonally-connected snake, which cannot touch itself, even diagonally (a cell is 'friendly' if it has a value identical to its row-, column- or box-number).  Cells connected by a dot are both friendly; if they are the same 'type' of friendly (that is, both match the row-number, both match the column-number, or both match the box-number) the dot is white, and otherwise the dot is grey.

title: Momentum equals GAS times Velocity
description:
Here are today's five Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 191 – Ultimaton by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/2p9fwyc2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given. Digits in cells separated by a V must sum to 5; digits in cells separated by an X must sum to 10. (No negative constraint - adjacent digits not separated by a letter can still sum to 5 or 10.)
GAS 192 – Greater Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5dabncfy 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. A circled value between two cells gives the greater of the two digits appearing in those cells. For instance, if a circle between two cells contains a 4, those cells might contain a 4 and a 3, or a 4 and a 1. 
GAS 193 – Diagonal Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/mv5xkuh9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, each marked diagonal must contain each of the digits from 1 to 9.
GAS 194 – X-23 by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/y86zhxv7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Orange regions are clones, and must contain the same digits in the same orientation. Digits in cells separated by an X must sum to 10. (No negative constraint - unmarked pairs of digits may sum to 10.)
GAS 195 – Average Sudoku by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/5mr95yvc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit in the central cell along a line must be the average of the two digits in the cells on the ends of the line. Be careful! In the correct solution, no rounding is required. :)
